     2	"""marathon-plan (Python path) — native planner CLI wrapper.
     3	
     4	GH-340: this used to shell out to the copied `utils/py/_marathon_plan_node.js` and hard-require
     5	`node`. It now drives the native Python engine in `utils/py/_marathon_plan.py` directly, so a
     6	production Python marathon-plan run needs neither Node nor that JS file. The former `docOf` and
     7	PR-review-overlay parity shims are folded into the native engine (no ROADMAP input mutation, no
     8	post-render patching).
     9	
    10	`utils/marathon-plan.sh` (Bash) remains the authoritative, dual-maintained twin per GH-308; this
    11	change does not alter the `XYZ_PYTHON=0` fallback.
    12	
    13	CLI contract (unchanged): [--dry-run | --check] [--policy quick-wins|derisk-first] [--deep]
    14	[--require-gh] [--format text|json]. `--zones-config` is translated to QUEUE_PLAN_ZONES_FILE by
    15	the Bash entry point before this script runs.
    16	"""
    17	import os
    18	import sys
    19	import subprocess
    20	import tempfile
    21	import shutil
    22	import datetime
    23	
    24	# Import the native engine relative to this file (utils/py/), independent of CWD/PYTHONPATH.
    25	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    26	import _marathon_plan as engine  # noqa: E402
    27	
    28	
    29	def die(msg):
    30	    sys.stderr.write(f"marathon-plan: {msg}\n")
    31	    sys.exit(2)
    32	
    33	
    34	def emit(msg):
    35	    sys.stderr.write(f"{msg}\n")
    36	
    37	
    38	def print_usage():
    39	    """Print the usage block to stdout and nothing else.
    40	
    41	    GH-349: this used to be inseparable from an unconditional `sys.exit(0)`, which made the `die()`
    42	    after the unknown-argument branch **unreachable** — so `marathon-plan.sh --bogus` exited 0 on the
    43	    default lane while the Bash twin exited 2. Splitting print from exit is the whole fix: Bash's
    44	    `usage()` (`utils/marathon-plan.sh:102`) also only prints, and its callers own the exit code.
    45	    """
    46	    print("""Usage: utils/py/marathon_plan.py [--dry-run | --check] [--policy quick-wins|derisk-first]
    47	                           [--deep] [--require-gh] [--format text|json]
    48	
    49	  (default)        Print the validation report and write PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-<today>.md.
    50	  --dry-run        Print the report; write no marathon-plan doc.
    51	  --check          Re-render and compare against today's marathon-plan doc; non-zero on drift. Writes nothing.
    52	  --policy P       quick-wins (default; momentum, low-cost first) | derisk-first (high-risk first).
    53	  --deep           Additionally delegate to utils/swarm-preflight.sh --dry-run per ready item
    54	                   (authoritative ref-based freshness/probe verdict; slower, needs network).
    55	  --require-gh     Treat an unavailable/offline `gh` as a hard error (exit 6) instead of degrading.
    56	  --format F       text (default) | json (findings as one JSON object per line).
    57	
    58	Exit: 0 clean · 2 usage · 3 ROADMAP unparseable · 4 drift present · 5 items held · 6 gh required-but-absent.""")
    59	
    60	
    61	def main():
    62	    policy = "quick-wins"
    63	    out_format = "text"
    64	    run_mode = "write"
    65	    deep = False
    66	    require_gh = False
    67	
    68	    args = sys.argv[1:]
    69	    i = 0
    70	    while i < len(args):
    71	        arg = args[i]
    72	        if arg == "--dry-run":
    73	            run_mode = "dry-run"
    74	            i += 1
    75	        elif arg == "--check":
    76	            run_mode = "check"
    77	            i += 1
    78	        elif arg == "--policy":
    79	            if i + 1 < len(args):
    80	                policy = args[i + 1]
    81	                i += 2
    82	            else:
    83	                die("missing argument for --policy")
    84	        elif arg == "--deep":
    85	            deep = True
    86	            i += 1
    87	        elif arg == "--require-gh":
    88	            require_gh = True
    89	            i += 1
    90	        elif arg == "--format":
    91	            if i + 1 < len(args):
    92	                out_format = args[i + 1]
    93	                i += 2
    94	            else:
    95	                die("missing argument for --format")
    96	        elif arg in ("--help", "-h"):
    97	            print_usage()

    99	        else:

   109	        die("--format must be 'text' or 'json'")

   111	    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
   112	    here_parent = os.path.dirname(here)

   114	
   115	    if is_vendored:

   117	        sp_cmd = ".xyz/utils/swarm-preflight.sh"

   119	        mp_cmd = ".xyz/utils/marathon-plan.sh"
   120	    else:
   121	        root = os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_ROOT", os.path.dirname(here_parent))
   122	        sp_cmd = "utils/swarm-preflight.sh"
   123	        md_cmd = "relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh"
   124	        mp_cmd = "utils/marathon-plan.sh"
   125	
   126	    roadmap = os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_ROADMAP", os.path.join(root, "ROADMAP.md"))
   127	    queue_dir = os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_QUEUE_DIR", os.path.join(root, "PROJECT", "2-WORKING"))
   128	
   129	    now = os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_NOW", datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"))
   130	    today = os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_TODAY", datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))
   131	
   132	    if not os.path.isfile(roadmap):
   133	        emit(f"ROADMAP not found: {roadmap}")
   134	        sys.exit(3)
   135	
   136	    tmp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="marathon-plan.")
   137	    render_out = os.path.join(tmp_dir, f"MARATHON-PLAN-{today}.md")
   138	    queue_doc = os.path.join(queue_dir, f"MARATHON-PLAN-{today}.md")
   139	
   140	    swarm_preflight = os.path.join(here_parent, "swarm-preflight.sh")
   141	    if not (deep and os.path.isfile(swarm_preflight) and os.access(swarm_preflight, os.X_OK)):
   142	        swarm_preflight = ""
   143	
   144	    # UTILS_DIR is the dir holding marathon-plan-zones.default.json — utils/ (parent of utils/py).
   145	    cfg = {
   146	        "root": root,
   147	        "roadmap": roadmap,
   148	        "queue_dir": queue_dir,
   149	        "today": today,
   150	        "now": now,
   151	        "policy": policy,
   152	        "format": out_format,
   153	        "deep": deep,
   154	        "require_gh": require_gh,
   155	        "swarm_preflight": swarm_preflight,
   156	        "sp_cmd": sp_cmd,
   157	        "md_cmd": md_cmd,
   158	        "mp_cmd": mp_cmd,
   159	        "utils_dir": here_parent,
   160	        "zones_config": os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_ZONES_CONFIG", ""),
   161	        "gh_state_file": os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_GH_STATE_FILE", ""),
   162	        "branches_file": os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_BRANCHES_FILE", ""),
   163	        "branch_env": os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_BRANCH", ""),
   164	        "gh_force": os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_GH", ""),
   165	        "base_files_file": os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_BASE_FILES_FILE", ""),
   166	        "zones_file_env": os.environ.get("QUEUE_PLAN_ZONES_FILE", ""),
   167	    }
   168	
   169	    try:
   170	        rc = engine.run(cfg, render_out)
   171	    except engine.ZoneConfigError as e:
   172	        sys.stderr.write(f"marathon-plan: {e}\n")
   173	        shutil.rmtree(tmp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
   174	        sys.exit(3)
   175	    except engine.EngineExit as e:
   176	        if e.message:
   177	            sys.stderr.write(f"{e.message}\n")

   179	        sys.exit(e.code)
   180	
   181	    if run_mode == "check":

   183	            emit(f"check: missing artifact: {os.path.relpath(queue_doc, root) if queue_doc.startswith(root) else queue_doc}")

   200	
   201	    os.makedirs(queue_dir, exist_ok=True)
   202	    shutil.copy2(render_out, queue_doc)
   203	
   204	    rel_doc = os.path.relpath(queue_doc, root) if queue_doc.startswith(root) else queue_doc
   205	    emit(f"wrote {rel_doc}")
   206	
   207	    shutil.rmtree(tmp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
   208	    sys.exit(rc)

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# FROZEN (GH-308): Python is authoritative — do not make behavior changes here.
     3	# Historical Bash fallback only; update utils/py/marathon_plan.py instead. See issue #308.
     4	# (The native engine behind that entry point is utils/py/_marathon_plan.py.)
     5	#
     6	# Frozen later than the other 11 — the exception was retired by GH-362.
     7	#
     8	# This file was GH-308's ONE documented exception: its Bash body stayed authoritative and
     9	# dual-maintained because the Python "port" shelled out to a copied, drifted node engine. GH-340
    10	# removed that reason — the copy is deleted, utils/py/_marathon_plan.py is a native stdlib engine,
    11	# and the Python lane needs no Node. `test/marathon-plan.sh` Scenario T still compares the two lanes
    12	# byte-for-byte (GH-348), so accidental drift is caught; the FIRST deliberate Python-only change to
    13	# the planner will fail it, and that failure is the signal to retire the assertion on purpose rather
    14	# than to quietly widen it.
    15	
    16	# GH-112 opt-in Python mode: XYZ_PYTHON=1 reroutes this entry point to the Python port in
    17	# utils/py/ (same CLI contract + exit codes). Default (unset/0) runs the canonical Bash
    18	# implementation below — Bash stays the supported default until the port is promoted.
    19	if [[ "${XYZ_PYTHON-1}" == "1" ]]; then
    20	  # UPGRADE.md §4 Phase-2 hardening (GH-255): (2a) `-` not `:-` so an explicit empty XYZ_PYTHON reads
    21	  # as not-1 → Bash (load-bearing once the default flips to 1); (2b) require python3 >=3.8 and fall
    22	  # back to Bash if missing/too-old. This site KEEPS its GH-154 --zones-config translation inside the
    23	  # guarded branch — do NOT collapse it to the generic shim (that would drop the zones-config block).
    24	  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    25	     && python3 -c 'import sys; raise SystemExit(0 if sys.version_info >= (3,8) else 1)' 2>/dev/null; then
    26	    _xyz_root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    27	    export XYZ_ROOT="$_xyz_root"
    28	    export PYTHONPATH="$_xyz_root/utils/py${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
    29	    _py_args=()
    30	    while (($# > 0)); do
    31	      case "$1" in
    32	        --zones-config)
    33	          [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { printf 'marathon-plan: missing argument for --zones-config\n' >&2; exit 2; }
    34	          export QUEUE_PLAN_ZONES_FILE="$2"
    35	          shift 2
    36	          ;;
    37	        *)
    38	          _py_args+=("$1")
    39	          shift
    40	          ;;
    41	      esac
    42	    done
    43	    exec python3 "$_xyz_root/utils/py/marathon_plan.py" "${_py_args[@]}"
    44	  else
    45	    echo "xyz: XYZ_PYTHON=1 but python3 missing or < 3.8 — falling back to Bash" >&2
    46	  fi
    47	fi
    48	
    49	# utils/marathon-plan.sh — deterministic "pre-pre-flight" queue planner.
    50	#
    51	# Reads the canonical ROADMAP.md ledger (a queue of work: GitHub issues + PROJECT/**.md docs),
    52	# validates each item is still real (not already fixed / silently half-done), factors in the PDDA
    53	# complexity/risk/effort ratings, and emits TWO artifacts:
    54	#
    55	#   1. a VALIDATION / DRIFT REPORT on stdout — deterministic signals, each a FLAG for a human,
    56	#      never an auto-fix (already-closed / already-landed / undocumented-partial / drift / unrated);
    57	#   2. a SEQUENCED marathon-plan doc  PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-YYYY-MM-DD.md — ratings-ranked, collision-lane
    58	#      aware, reproducing the shape of the hand-authored QUEUE-2026-06-27.md.
    59	#
    60	# It is the stage BEFORE utils/swarm-preflight.sh (which is per-item readiness). Overlap is intended:
    61	# this planner REUSES swarm-preflight's contract shape + probe semantics, and can DELEGATE to it
    62	# per-item with --deep. The planner is a PRODUCER of a plan; it never executes a marathon
    63	# (GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md §8 — the operator decides).
    64	#
    65	# Determinism: the score for every item is printed alongside its inputs so any ordering is
    66	# reproducible by hand. Same ledger + same ratings + same NOW/TODAY ⇒ byte-identical output
    67	# (which is what makes the manual --check drift comparison below meaningful).
    68	#
    69	# Usage:
    70	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh                         # report on stdout + write today's marathon-plan doc
    71	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --dry-run               # report only; write nothing
    72	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --check                 # exit non-zero if today's marathon-plan doc is out of sync
    73	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --policy derisk-first   # high-risk work sorts earlier (default: quick-wins)
    74	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --deep                  # also delegate to swarm-preflight --dry-run per item
    75	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --format json           # findings as JSON lines (pdda finding shape)
    76	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --zones-config FILE     # explicit zone-rules override
    77	#
    78	# Exit: 0 clean · 2 usage · 3 ROADMAP missing/unparseable ·
    79	#       4 emitted, drift present (already-landed/closed — reconcile the ledger) ·
    80	#       5 emitted, items held out of sequencing (unrated / note-only / not-ready) ·
    81	#       6 gh required but unavailable (--require-gh only).
    82	#
    83	# Test seam (all optional; unset in production):
    84	#   QUEUE_PLAN_ROOT / QUEUE_PLAN_ROADMAP / QUEUE_PLAN_QUEUE_DIR / QUEUE_PLAN_NOW / QUEUE_PLAN_TODAY
    85	#   QUEUE_PLAN_GH_STATE_FILE   JSON map {"24":"CLOSED",...} used instead of calling `gh` (hermetic)
    86	#   QUEUE_PLAN_BRANCHES_FILE   newline list of branch names used instead of calling `git branch`
    87	#   QUEUE_PLAN_GH              force gh mode: off|stub (off ⇒ gh-unverified; stub needs *_STATE_FILE)
    88	#   QUEUE_PLAN_ZONES_FILE      planner zone-rules override (2nd-precedence tier; see --zones-config)
    89	
    90	set -uo pipefail
    91	# strict-mode: -e exempt — analysis tool with expected-nonzero probes (git/gh/grep); errors handled explicitly. See GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md#strict-mode-policy.
    92	
    93	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    94	# Vendored install: HERE is <target>/.xyz/utils → parent is .xyz → target root is grandparent.
    95	_here_parent="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
    96	if [ "$(basename "$_here_parent")" = ".xyz" ]; then
    97	  ROOT="${QUEUE_PLAN_ROOT:-"$(cd "$_here_parent/.." && pwd)"}"
    98	  _SP_CMD=".xyz/utils/swarm-preflight.sh"
    99	  _MD_CMD=".xyz/relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh"
   100	  _MP_CMD=".xyz/utils/marathon-plan.sh"
   101	else
   102	  ROOT="${QUEUE_PLAN_ROOT:-"$_here_parent"}"
   103	  _SP_CMD="utils/swarm-preflight.sh"
   104	  _MD_CMD="relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh"
   105	  _MP_CMD="utils/marathon-plan.sh"
   106	fi
   107	ROADMAP="${QUEUE_PLAN_ROADMAP:-"$ROOT/ROADMAP.md"}"
   108	QUEUE_DIR="${QUEUE_PLAN_QUEUE_DIR:-"$ROOT/PROJECT/2-WORKING"}"
   109	NOW="${QUEUE_PLAN_NOW:-"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"}"
   110	TODAY="${QUEUE_PLAN_TODAY:-"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%d)"}"
   111	
   112	die()  { printf 'marathon-plan: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 2; }
   113	emit() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
   114	
   115	usage() {
   116	  cat <<'EOF'
   117	Usage: utils/marathon-plan.sh [--dry-run | --check] [--policy quick-wins|derisk-first]
   118	                           [--deep] [--require-gh] [--format text|json]
   119	                           [--zones-config <file>]
   120	
   121	  (default)        Print the validation report and write PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-<today>.md.
   122	  --dry-run        Print the report; write no marathon-plan doc.
   123	  --check          Re-render and compare against today's marathon-plan doc; non-zero on drift. Writes nothing.
   124	  --policy P       quick-wins (default; momentum, low-cost first) | derisk-first (high-risk first).
   125	  --deep           Additionally delegate to utils/swarm-preflight.sh --dry-run per ready item
   126	                   (authoritative ref-based freshness/probe verdict; slower, needs network).
   127	  --require-gh     Treat an unavailable/offline `gh` as a hard error (exit 6) instead of degrading.
   128	  --format F       text (default) | json (findings as one JSON object per line).
   129	  --zones-config   Explicit planner zone-rules override. Relative paths resolve from the caller CWD.
   130	
   131	Exit: 0 clean · 2 usage · 3 ROADMAP unparseable · 4 drift present · 5 items held · 6 gh required-but-absent.
   132	EOF
   133	}
   134	
   135	POLICY="quick-wins"
   136	FORMAT="text"
   137	RUN_MODE="write"     # write | dry-run | check
   138	DEEP=0
   139	REQUIRE_GH=0
   140	ZONES_CONFIG=""
   141	
   142	while (($# > 0)); do
   143	  case "$1" in
   144	    --dry-run)    RUN_MODE="dry-run"; shift ;;
   145	    --check)      RUN_MODE="check"; shift ;;
   146	    --policy)     POLICY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
   147	    --deep)       DEEP=1; shift ;;
   148	    --require-gh) REQUIRE_GH=1; shift ;;
   149	    --format)     FORMAT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
   150	    --zones-config) ZONES_CONFIG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
   151	    --help|-h)    usage; exit 0 ;;
   152	    *)            usage; die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
   153	  esac
   154	done
   155	
   156	case "$POLICY" in quick-wins|derisk-first) ;; *) die "--policy must be 'quick-wins' or 'derisk-first'" ;; esac
   157	case "$FORMAT" in text|json) ;; *) die "--format must be 'text' or 'json'" ;; esac
   158	[[ -f "$ROADMAP" ]] || { emit "ROADMAP not found: $ROADMAP"; exit 3; }
   159	command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "node is required (Node stdlib only; no deps) but not found in PATH"

   161	TMP="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/marathon-plan.XXXXXX")"
   162	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
   163	RENDER_OUT="$TMP/MARATHON-PLAN-$TODAY.md"
   164	QUEUE_DOC="$QUEUE_DIR/MARATHON-PLAN-$TODAY.md"

   166	# Resolve the swarm-preflight path for --deep delegation (skipped silently if absent).
   167	SWARM_PREFLIGHT="$HERE/swarm-preflight.sh"
   168	[[ "$DEEP" -eq 1 && -x "$SWARM_PREFLIGHT" ]] || SWARM_PREFLIGHT=""

   176	QP_DEEP="$DEEP" QP_REQUIRE_GH="$REQUIRE_GH" QP_SWARM_PREFLIGHT="$SWARM_PREFLIGHT" \

   292	    sourcePath,
   293	    zones,
   294	    defaultZone: {

   296	      penalty: Number.isFinite(Number(raw.defaultZone.penalty)) ? Number(raw.defaultZone.penalty) : 0,

   367	// Frontmatter line reader — same simple `key: value` contract pdda-lib.sh enforces.
   368	function frontmatter(doc) {

   372	  let i = 0;
   373	  while (i < lines.length && lines[i].trim() === "") i++;

   375	  const fm = {};
   376	  for (i++; i < lines.length; i++) {

   378	    const m = lines[i].match(/^([A-Za-z0-9_]+):\s*(.*)$/);
   379	    if (m) fm[m[1]] = m[2].trim();
   380	  }
   381	  return fm;
   382	}

   384	// Extract a swarm-preflight contract (heading /preflight contract/i + fenced ```json) — same shape
   385	// utils/swarm-preflight.sh reads. Returns the parsed object or null (planner degrades, never dies).
   386	function extractContract(doc) {
   387	  const raw = readFileSafe(doc);
   388	  if (raw == null) return null;
   389	  const lines = raw.split(/\r?\n/);
   390	  const h = lines.findIndex((l) => /^#{1,6}\s+.*preflight\s+contract/i.test(l));
   391	  if (h < 0) return null;
   392	  let start = -1;
   393	  for (let j = h + 1; j < lines.length; j++) {
   394	    if (/^```json\s*$/i.test(lines[j])) { start = j + 1; break; }
   395	    if (/^#{1,6}\s+/.test(lines[j])) break;
   396	  }
   397	  if (start < 0) return null;
   398	  let end = -1;
   399	  for (let j = start; j < lines.length; j++) { if (/^```\s*$/.test(lines[j])) { end = j; break; } }

   404	// Probe evaluator — same verdict semantics as swarm-preflight's eval-probes.mjs, run LOCALLY against
   405	// ROOT (cheap, offline). landed = already fixed; unfixed = fix still required; blocked = can't tell.
   406	function evalProbe(p) {
   407	  const at = (rel) => path.resolve(ROOT, rel || "");

   409	    switch (p.type) {
   410	      case "path_absent":  return fs.existsSync(at(p.path)) ? "landed" : "unfixed";
   411	      case "path_present": return !fs.existsSync(at(p.path)) ? "blocked" : "unfixed";
   412	      case "grep_present":
   413	        if (!fs.existsSync(at(p.path))) return "blocked";
   414	        return new RegExp(p.pattern).test(fs.readFileSync(at(p.path), "utf8")) ? "unfixed" : "landed";
   415	      case "grep_absent":
   416	        return (fs.existsSync(at(p.path)) && new RegExp(p.pattern).test(fs.readFileSync(at(p.path), "utf8")))
   417	          ? "landed" : "unfixed";
   418	      default: return "blocked";
   419	    }
   420	  } catch { return "blocked"; }
   421	}

   501	// GH-86: parse a "## Lanes" markdown table from the manual PR-review-queue overlay doc

   531	// ── item resolution ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

   603	// GH-5: a "contract seam" is a directory two lanes SHARE (deeper than a top-level dir) even though

    49	# utils/marathon-plan.sh — deterministic "pre-pre-flight" queue planner.
    50	#
    51	# Reads the canonical ROADMAP.md ledger (a queue of work: GitHub issues + PROJECT/**.md docs),
    52	# validates each item is still real (not already fixed / silently half-done), factors in the PDDA
    53	# complexity/risk/effort ratings, and emits TWO artifacts:
    54	#
    55	#   1. a VALIDATION / DRIFT REPORT on stdout — deterministic signals, each a FLAG for a human,
    56	#      never an auto-fix (already-closed / already-landed / undocumented-partial / drift / unrated);
    57	#   2. a SEQUENCED marathon-plan doc  PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-YYYY-MM-DD.md — ratings-ranked, collision-lane
    58	#      aware, reproducing the shape of the hand-authored QUEUE-2026-06-27.md.
    59	#
    60	# It is the stage BEFORE utils/swarm-preflight.sh (which is per-item readiness). Overlap is intended:
    61	# this planner REUSES swarm-preflight's contract shape + probe semantics, and can DELEGATE to it
    62	# per-item with --deep. The planner is a PRODUCER of a plan; it never executes a marathon
    63	# (GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md §8 — the operator decides).
    64	#
    65	# Determinism: the score for every item is printed alongside its inputs so any ordering is
    66	# reproducible by hand. Same ledger + same ratings + same NOW/TODAY ⇒ byte-identical output
    67	# (which is what makes the manual --check drift comparison below meaningful).
    68	#
    69	# Usage:
    70	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh                         # report on stdout + write today's marathon-plan doc
    71	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --dry-run               # report only; write nothing
    72	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --check                 # exit non-zero if today's marathon-plan doc is out of sync
    73	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --policy derisk-first   # high-risk work sorts earlier (default: quick-wins)
    74	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --deep                  # also delegate to swarm-preflight --dry-run per item
    75	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --format json           # findings as JSON lines (pdda finding shape)
    76	#   utils/marathon-plan.sh --zones-config FILE     # explicit zone-rules override
    77	#
    78	# Exit: 0 clean · 2 usage · 3 ROADMAP missing/unparseable ·
    79	#       4 emitted, drift present (already-landed/closed — reconcile the ledger) ·
    80	#       5 emitted, items held out of sequencing (unrated / note-only / not-ready) ·
    81	#       6 gh required but unavailable (--require-gh only).
    82	#
    83	# Test seam (all optional; unset in production):
    84	#   QUEUE_PLAN_ROOT / QUEUE_PLAN_ROADMAP / QUEUE_PLAN_QUEUE_DIR / QUEUE_PLAN_NOW / QUEUE_PLAN_TODAY
    85	#   QUEUE_PLAN_GH_STATE_FILE   JSON map {"24":"CLOSED",...} used instead of calling `gh` (hermetic)
    86	#   QUEUE_PLAN_BRANCHES_FILE   newline list of branch names used instead of calling `git branch`
    87	#   QUEUE_PLAN_GH              force gh mode: off|stub (off ⇒ gh-unverified; stub needs *_STATE_FILE)
    88	#   QUEUE_PLAN_ZONES_FILE      planner zone-rules override (2nd-precedence tier; see --zones-config)

README.md-85-2. **Relay** — an iterative, turn-based loop between two agents on one shared file: a **Producer**
README.md:86:   builds an artifact, a **Reviewer** critiques and proposes fixes, and they hand off back and
README.md:87:   forth until the artifact converges. This replaces you copy-pasting output between two agent
README.md:88:   windows. Changes are confined to the relay thread file and the artifact under review.
README.md-89-3. **Swarm** — two or more agents working **concurrently** on the same repo, each claiming a
README.md-90-   non-overlapping, path-scoped lane (via the `tick` kernel) so they never collide. Good for
README.md-91-   parallel builds or parallel codebase recon. This is where PDDA's doc structure starts to matter,
README.md-92-   because lanes are carved from well-defined task docs.
README.md-93-4. **Marathon** — the full automation payoff: a queue of pre-flighted tasks (built up during the
README.md-94-   day) fired as one long autonomous run, typically end-of-day or overnight. Marathon **requires**
README.md:95:   PDDA, because the preflight scripts rely on PDDA's opinionated docs/roadmap structure to verify
README.md-96-   every queued task is well-specified before anything runs unattended.

README.md-184-
README.md-185-PDDA's folder structure is deliberately opinionated. That setup cost is the trade for what
README.md-186-Marathon gives you: because every task lives in a predictable doc structure, the system can
README.md:187:preflight, queue, and execute a full day's work without you babysitting it. If that trade doesn't
README.md-188-appeal yet, stay on the fast path — Relay and Consult deliver value on day one with zero
README.md-189-restructuring.

README.md-213-will read as more than it says. The precise answer:
README.md-214-
README.md-215-**What matches.** Phases are real nodes — each gets `marathon-system/<id>/RELAY.md`, a tick token, a
README.md:216:reviewer, a brief, and an artifact allowlist, with an LLM turn as the body. Inside a phase there is
README.md-217-a genuine LLM-selected edge: the reviewer writes `STATUS:`, and `utils/py/relay_drive.py` treats
README.md-218-`Approved`/`Closed` as terminal and anything else as another round, bounded by a round cap. Every
README.md-219-phase boundary runs a verification gate, which must be able to *start* before turn 1 — a missing
--
README.md-224-**What doesn't.** There is no DAG. `depends_on` is scalar-only — one dependency per phase — so a
README.md-225-join is inexpressible: "p4 after p2 *and* p3" cannot be written. There is no parallel execution;
README.md-226-`relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml` states that phases run strictly one at a time and that a
README.md:227:disjoint write-set does not buy you parallelism. `depends_on` **validates** the order you authored
README.md-228-rather than **deriving** one, which inverts the usual graph model. And a failure halts the chain —
README.md-229-there is no conditional edge to a remediation node.
README.md-230-
README.md-231-So: a sequential chain of agent-driven build→review loops, with hard gates at every boundary. The
README.md-232-scheduling a graph engine exists to automate is handed to the operator on purpose — see
README.md:233:`GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md` §8, and `utils/swarm-preflight.sh`, which is the *producer* of a run packet
README.md-234-and never its executor.
README.md-235-
README.md-236-Parallelism does exist, but as **swarms**: separate agents in separate worktrees or clones on
README.md:237:disjoint write-sets, coordinated by `tick` locks. That is arranged by the operator, not scheduled
README.md-238-from a dependency graph.
README.md-239-
README.md-240-### Do phases run in parallel? What does `depends_on` actually do?

README.md-273-- `relay-system/` — relay transcripts, reviews, and dogfood runs.
README.md-274-- `PROJECT/2-WORKING/` — active project docs and working plans.
README.md-275-- `bin/tick`, `src/`, `test/` — the `tick` coordination kernel and its test suite.
README.md:276:- `utils/swarm-preflight.sh` — marathon intake planner: turns a project doc or a GH-issue bundle into a marathon-ready run packet (freshness + fix-still-required checks, readiness gate, Codex/agy lane plan). Run `utils/swarm-preflight.sh --help`; see [GH-25-SWARM-PREFLIGHT-PLANNER.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-25-SWARM-PREFLIGHT-PLANNER.md).
README.md:277:- `utils/marathon-plan.sh` — the marathon planner/ranker: scores the whole ROADMAP ledger into waves of disjoint, collision-safe write-sets, and with `--deep` delegates to `swarm-preflight.sh --dry-run` per item for an authoritative freshness verdict. Writes `PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-<date>.md` — the "marathon file" the operator skills act on.
README.md:278:- `utils/swe-diagram/` — dependency-free architecture/Git-history diagram generator; `layout: "git-lanes"` renders stacked branch lanes with commits left-to-right, driven by a local ref-reading generator that emits an auditable JSON spec plus self-contained HTML. See [GH-201](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/201).
README.md-279-- `utils/git-bundle-snapshot.sh` + `relay-automation/hooks/gh177-sandbox-test-guard.sh` — the wipe-prevention layer: rotated `git bundle --all` backups on a daily cron, plus a PreToolUse hook that blocks running the test suite under a *sandboxed* Claude Code Bash call (the ignition for the GH-177 repo wipes). See [GH-233](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/233).
README.md-280-- `install.sh` — materializes the `tick` runtime (`bin/tick` + `src/*.js`) into an external repo and records the install in a per-user, machine-local registry (`~/.config/xyz/registry.tsv`). See "Install into another repo" below.
README.md-281-- `utils/hq/` — **HQ**, the multi-repo command center (`hq.sh` + `hq-lib.sh`); driven by the user-level `/hq` skill in `skills/hq/`. See [HQ — multi-repo command center](#hq--multi-repo-command-center) below.

README.md-347-| `hq.sh park [--create] [--title T] <project> <req…>` | **Issue-first intake** in the target repo: GH issue → `PROJECT/1-INBOX/` capture → ROADMAP parking. Previews unless `--create`. |
README.md-348-| `hq.sh promote [--create] --gh-issue N <project>` | **PDDA `1-INBOX → 2-WORKING`** (GH-138): `git mv GH-N-*.md` + scaffold the moved doc so it satisfies the enforced 2-WORKING contract (leaves ratings/QA gates as operator TODOs). Previews unless `--create`. |
README.md-349-| `hq.sh queue [--create] [--gh-issue N] <project> <req…>` | Append an **HQ-queued lane** to the target's newest `MARATHON-*.md` plan (non-destructive). Previews unless `--create`. |
README.md:350:| `hq.sh fire --gh-issue N [--risk 1-5] <project>` | **Gated prepare-and-hand-off** — resolves, gates (Tier A, `risk < 3`), and emits the `swarm-preflight` command for the operator to run. Never drives the harness (GUIDING-PRINCIPLES §8). |
README.md-351-
README.md-352-The intake-to-dispatch pipeline is **`park → promote → queue → fire`** — capture on the rails, promote
README.md-353-into active work, queue a marathon lane, then hand off. Each step previews first.

README.md-82-1. **Consult** — a one-shot, parallel second opinion. The same question fans out to Codex and agy
README.md-83-   at the same time, each answers independently in an isolated copy of the repo, and the answers
README.md-84-   are reconciled into one. Nothing is modified; it's purely advisory. Lowest risk, fastest payoff.
README.md-85-2. **Relay** — an iterative, turn-based loop between two agents on one shared file: a **Producer**
README.md:86:   builds an artifact, a **Reviewer** critiques and proposes fixes, and they hand off back and
README.md:87:   forth until the artifact converges. This replaces you copy-pasting output between two agent
README.md:88:   windows. Changes are confined to the relay thread file and the artifact under review.
README.md-89-3. **Swarm** — two or more agents working **concurrently** on the same repo, each claiming a
README.md-90-   non-overlapping, path-scoped lane (via the `tick` kernel) so they never collide. Good for
README.md-91-   parallel builds or parallel codebase recon. This is where PDDA's doc structure starts to matter,
README.md-92-   because lanes are carved from well-defined task docs.
README.md-93-4. **Marathon** — the full automation payoff: a queue of pre-flighted tasks (built up during the
README.md-94-   day) fired as one long autonomous run, typically end-of-day or overnight. Marathon **requires**
README.md:95:   PDDA, because the preflight scripts rely on PDDA's opinionated docs/roadmap structure to verify
README.md-96-   every queued task is well-specified before anything runs unattended.
README.md-97-
README.md-98-How they fit together: **Consult** answers "what do the other models think?", **Relay** answers
README.md-99-"build this and have it reviewed until it's right", **Swarm** answers "do several independent

README.md-114-- **What each step actually touches** (so you know how to undo it):
README.md-115-  - *Skill install* — symlinks skill folders into `~/.claude/skills/` (user-level). A `git pull` in your XYZ clone will silently update your installed skills. Undo: delete those symlinks. Your repos are untouched.
README.md:116:  - *Relay runs* — write a dated thread file under `relay-system/<date>/` plus the artifact being
README.md-117-    reviewed, on your branch. Undo: discard the branch.
README.md-118-  - *Consult runs* — advisory only; agents work in isolated copies. Nothing to undo. **Known
README.md-119-    limitation:** the `agy` CLI has been observed grounding its answers against the real repo
README.md-120-    instead of confining itself to its isolated copy, undermining the "isolated" guarantee for that

README.md-183-### Important note on PDDA's structure
README.md-184-
README.md-185-PDDA's folder structure is deliberately opinionated. That setup cost is the trade for what
README.md-186-Marathon gives you: because every task lives in a predictable doc structure, the system can
README.md:187:preflight, queue, and execute a full day's work without you babysitting it. If that trade doesn't
README.md-188-appeal yet, stay on the fast path — Relay and Consult deliver value on day one with zero
README.md-189-restructuring.
README.md-190-
README.md-191----
--
README.md-198-- **`tick`** — the coordination kernel: a shared local event log (`.tick/events/`) that agents
README.md-199-  claim work through, serialized by an `O_EXCL` lock.
README.md-200-- **relay** — a turn-based loop where one agent builds and another reviews, handing off through
README.md-201-  files instead of a human copy-pasting between windows.
README.md:202:- **Marathon** (`relay-automation/marathon.sh`) — chains several relay build→review phases from a
README.md:203:  `MARATHON.yaml`, in `depends_on` order. The multi-agent coordinator built on the relay loop.
README.md-204-- **agy** — the Antigravity CLI (Google), one of the agents XYZ coordinates alongside Claude Code
README.md-205-  and Codex.
README.md-206-
README.md-207-## FAQ
--
README.md-212-vocabulary (a DAG of nodes and edges, parallel stages, routing decisions), the Glossary entry above
README.md-213-will read as more than it says. The precise answer:
README.md-214-
README.md-215-**What matches.** Phases are real nodes — each gets `marathon-system/<id>/RELAY.md`, a tick token, a
README.md:216:reviewer, a brief, and an artifact allowlist, with an LLM turn as the body. Inside a phase there is
README.md-217-a genuine LLM-selected edge: the reviewer writes `STATUS:`, and `utils/py/relay_drive.py` treats
README.md-218-`Approved`/`Closed` as terminal and anything else as another round, bounded by a round cap. Every
README.md:219:phase boundary runs a verification gate, which must be able to *start* before turn 1 — a missing
README.md-220-gate fails fast rather than being skipped. And the whole run is an inspectable state machine
README.md-221-(`.tick/events/`, `RELAY.md`, `ESCALATION.md` with typed reason codes) rather than a model's
README.md-222-self-report.
README.md-223-
README.md:224:**What doesn't.** There is no DAG. `depends_on` is scalar-only — one dependency per phase — so a
README.md-225-join is inexpressible: "p4 after p2 *and* p3" cannot be written. There is no parallel execution;
README.md:226:`relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml` states that phases run strictly one at a time and that a
README.md:227:disjoint write-set does not buy you parallelism. `depends_on` **validates** the order you authored
README.md-228-rather than **deriving** one, which inverts the usual graph model. And a failure halts the chain —
README.md-229-there is no conditional edge to a remediation node.
README.md-230-
README.md-231-So: a sequential chain of agent-driven build→review loops, with hard gates at every boundary. The
README.md-232-scheduling a graph engine exists to automate is handed to the operator on purpose — see
README.md:233:`GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md` §8, and `utils/swarm-preflight.sh`, which is the *producer* of a run packet
README.md-234-and never its executor.
README.md-235-
README.md-236-Parallelism does exist, but as **swarms**: separate agents in separate worktrees or clones on
README.md:237:disjoint write-sets, coordinated by `tick` locks. That is arranged by the operator, not scheduled
README.md-238-from a dependency graph.
README.md-239-
README.md:240:### Do phases run in parallel? What does `depends_on` actually do?
README.md-241-
README.md-242-No, and less than you'd think. Phases run **one at a time**, in the order they appear in the plan.
README.md:243:A phase *without* `depends_on` is not "unordered" or "parallel-safe" — it simply runs when its turn
README.md:244:comes. `depends_on` constrains that order; it does not create it.
README.md-245-
README.md:246:It also takes exactly one phase id, unquoted (`depends_on: p3`). The list form `depends_on: [p3]`
README.md:247:parses as the literal string and aborts the plan with an unknown-phase error that points at your
README.md:248:phase ids rather than at the field's shape. Chain them (`p3 → p4 → p5`) to express a longer order.
README.md-249-
README.md:250:Analysing your phases for a disjoint write-set is still worth doing — it is how you learn which
README.md:251:phases genuinely need `depends_on` — but it will not make them concurrent.
README.md-252-
README.md-253-Always `--dry-run` a new plan first. It parses every field and prints the real execution order at
README.md-254-zero cost, which is the cheapest way to catch both a mis-shaped field and a wrong mental model.
README.md-255-
--
README.md-262-  Claude Code only scans `~/.claude/skills/`, so a fresh clone won't see these until you symlink them in —
README.md-263-  run `bash skills/relay-xyz/install.sh` once per clone/machine to make the `/relay-xyz` skill discoverable
README.md-264-  (see [skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md](skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md#first-time-setup-on-a-new-clone-or-machine-make-the-skill-discoverable)).
README.md-265-- `skills/marathon-triage/`, `skills/marathon-cleanup/`, `skills/10days/` — the marathon operator
README.md:266:  skills: triage PDDA intake + active work into a ranked, preflight-checked, collision-safe queue
README.md-267-  ([`marathon-triage`](skills/marathon-triage/SKILL.md)); archive only lanes with verified completion
README.md-268-  evidence after a run ([`marathon-cleanup`](skills/marathon-cleanup/SKILL.md)); and — the one deliberate,
README.md-269-  operator-authorized auto-fire exception to the "ask before firing" rule — sweep recent GitHub issues into
README.md-270-  a marathon and execute it unattended ([`10days`](skills/10days/SKILL.md)). See [GH-240](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/240).
--
README.md-272-  (GH issue + capture doc + ROADMAP park), without touching the repo you're standing in.
README.md-273-- `relay-system/` — relay transcripts, reviews, and dogfood runs.
README.md-274-- `PROJECT/2-WORKING/` — active project docs and working plans.
README.md-275-- `bin/tick`, `src/`, `test/` — the `tick` coordination kernel and its test suite.
README.md:276:- `utils/swarm-preflight.sh` — marathon intake planner: turns a project doc or a GH-issue bundle into a marathon-ready run packet (freshness + fix-still-required checks, readiness gate, Codex/agy lane plan). Run `utils/swarm-preflight.sh --help`; see [GH-25-SWARM-PREFLIGHT-PLANNER.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-25-SWARM-PREFLIGHT-PLANNER.md).
README.md:277:- `utils/marathon-plan.sh` — the marathon planner/ranker: scores the whole ROADMAP ledger into waves of disjoint, collision-safe write-sets, and with `--deep` delegates to `swarm-preflight.sh --dry-run` per item for an authoritative freshness verdict. Writes `PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-<date>.md` — the "marathon file" the operator skills act on.
README.md-278-- `utils/swe-diagram/` — dependency-free architecture/Git-history diagram generator; `layout: "git-lanes"` renders stacked branch lanes with commits left-to-right, driven by a local ref-reading generator that emits an auditable JSON spec plus self-contained HTML. See [GH-201](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/201).
README.md-279-- `utils/git-bundle-snapshot.sh` + `relay-automation/hooks/gh177-sandbox-test-guard.sh` — the wipe-prevention layer: rotated `git bundle --all` backups on a daily cron, plus a PreToolUse hook that blocks running the test suite under a *sandboxed* Claude Code Bash call (the ignition for the GH-177 repo wipes). See [GH-233](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/233).
README.md-280-- `install.sh` — materializes the `tick` runtime (`bin/tick` + `src/*.js`) into an external repo and records the install in a per-user, machine-local registry (`~/.config/xyz/registry.tsv`). See "Install into another repo" below.
README.md-281-- `utils/hq/` — **HQ**, the multi-repo command center (`hq.sh` + `hq-lib.sh`); driven by the user-level `/hq` skill in `skills/hq/`. See [HQ — multi-repo command center](#hq--multi-repo-command-center) below.
--
README.md-346-| `hq.sh next [--limit N]` | **Priority board** — projects ranked by Rebalance `priority_tier` with each one's HQ capability tier. Read-only. |
README.md-347-| `hq.sh park [--create] [--title T] <project> <req…>` | **Issue-first intake** in the target repo: GH issue → `PROJECT/1-INBOX/` capture → ROADMAP parking. Previews unless `--create`. |
README.md-348-| `hq.sh promote [--create] --gh-issue N <project>` | **PDDA `1-INBOX → 2-WORKING`** (GH-138): `git mv GH-N-*.md` + scaffold the moved doc so it satisfies the enforced 2-WORKING contract (leaves ratings/QA gates as operator TODOs). Previews unless `--create`. |
README.md-349-| `hq.sh queue [--create] [--gh-issue N] <project> <req…>` | Append an **HQ-queued lane** to the target's newest `MARATHON-*.md` plan (non-destructive). Previews unless `--create`. |
README.md:350:| `hq.sh fire --gh-issue N [--risk 1-5] <project>` | **Gated prepare-and-hand-off** — resolves, gates (Tier A, `risk < 3`), and emits the `swarm-preflight` command for the operator to run. Never drives the harness (GUIDING-PRINCIPLES §8). |
README.md-351-
README.md-352-The intake-to-dispatch pipeline is **`park → promote → queue → fire`** — capture on the rails, promote
README.md-353-into active work, queue a marathon lane, then hand off. Each step previews first.
README.md-354-

relay-automation/marathon.sh-1-#!/usr/bin/env bash
relay-automation/marathon.sh-2-set -euo pipefail
relay-automation/marathon.sh-3-#
relay-automation/marathon.sh:4:# marathon.sh — Phase 4 (M5): multi-phase orchestrator. Reads MARATHON.yaml, resolves depends_on
relay-automation/marathon.sh:5:# order, and runs each phase through marathon-drive.sh (the unmodified single-phase loop). Advances
relay-automation/marathon.sh:6:# on phase approval; HALTS on the first phase failure (relay no-progress / cap / gate / containment),
relay-automation/marathon.sh:7:# leaving that phase's ESCALATION.md (written by marathon-drive) and NOT starting later phases.
relay-automation/marathon.sh:8:# Emits marathon.complete only when every phase is approved.
relay-automation/marathon.sh-9-#
relay-automation/marathon.sh:10:# Per-phase round cap = 2 * max_review_rounds + 1 (turns ≠ rounds; the off-by-one kills phases early).
relay-automation/marathon.sh:11:# Cross-phase context injection (M6) and MARATHON-STATE.md projection (M7) are deliberately deferred —
relay-automation/marathon.sh:12:# the boundary events already land in .tick/events/ (phase.start/approved/escalated, marathon.complete).
relay-automation/marathon.sh-13-#
relay-automation/marathon.sh-14-# Usage:
relay-automation/marathon.sh:15:#   relay-automation/marathon.sh --plan MARATHON.yaml [--builder codex] [--phases-dir DIR]
relay-automation/marathon.sh-16-#                                [--pre-advance-cmd CMD] [--dry-run] [--retry PHASE-ID]
relay-automation/marathon.sh-17-#
relay-automation/marathon.sh-18-# GH-212: default builder is `codex` — no per-call API charge (bills via the Codex/ChatGPT
relay-automation/marathon.sh-19-# subscription; agy is the other cost-blind option). `--builder claude` spawns a headless Claude
relay-automation/marathon.sh-20-# Code CLI subprocess instead: a SEPARATE, PER-CALL API-BILLED turn-taker, distinct from an

     4	# marathon.sh — Phase 4 (M5): multi-phase orchestrator. Reads MARATHON.yaml, resolves depends_on
     5	# order, and runs each phase through marathon-drive.sh (the unmodified single-phase loop). Advances
     6	# on phase approval; HALTS on the first phase failure (relay no-progress / cap / gate / containment),
     7	# leaving that phase's ESCALATION.md (written by marathon-drive) and NOT starting later phases.
     8	# Emits marathon.complete only when every phase is approved.
     9	#
    10	# Per-phase round cap = 2 * max_review_rounds + 1 (turns ≠ rounds; the off-by-one kills phases early).
    11	# Cross-phase context injection (M6) and MARATHON-STATE.md projection (M7) are deliberately deferred —
    12	# the boundary events already land in .tick/events/ (phase.start/approved/escalated, marathon.complete).
    13	#
    14	# Usage:
    15	#   relay-automation/marathon.sh --plan MARATHON.yaml [--builder codex] [--phases-dir DIR]
    16	#                                [--pre-advance-cmd CMD] [--dry-run] [--retry PHASE-ID]
    17	#
    18	# GH-212: default builder is `codex` — no per-call API charge (bills via the Codex/ChatGPT
    19	# subscription; agy is the other cost-blind option). `--builder claude` spawns a headless Claude
    20	# Code CLI subprocess instead: a SEPARATE, PER-CALL API-BILLED turn-taker, distinct from an
    21	# interactive session. Use it only as an explicit, cost-acknowledged choice.
    22	#
    23	# GH-212: a plan's `--plan` YAML (+ its phase briefs) must resolve under PROJECT/2-WORKING/ in the
    24	# target repo — not a standalone top-level folder (e.g. marathon-plans/<slug>/) an agent might
    25	# pattern-match from a prior repo. Exempt: paths under this harness's own home (MARATHON_HOME —
    26	# covers shipped examples like MARATHON.example.yaml). Override: MARATHON_ALLOW_PLAN_OUTSIDE_WORKING=1.
    27	#
    28	# GH-116: --retry <phase-id> recovers a phase whose relay task was left open/never-claimed
    29	# (permanently spent, per this repo's claim-then-abandon constraint) WITHOUT manually renaming the
    30	# phase id in MARATHON.yaml. It overrides just that one phase's --relay-task with the first unused
    31	# MARATHON-<ID>-TURN-<N> suffix (N starts at 2, checked via `tick info`) — every other phase derives
    32	# its task name exactly as before. marathon-drive.sh already supports --relay-task natively; this is
    33	# purely a marathon.sh-side task-name override, no change to marathon-drive.sh itself.
    34	#
    35	# The MARATHON.yaml phase fields drive each marathon-drive call: id→--phase-id, reviewer→--reviewer,
    36	# brief→--phase-brief (required to run), artifact→--artifact, turn_timeout_s→RELAY_TURN_TIMEOUT_S,
    37	# max_review_rounds→--round-cap.
    38	#
    39	# Environment overrides (for tests):
    40	#   MARATHON_HOME       — harness home (default: parent of this script's dir)
    41	#   MARATHON_ROOT       — target repo root (default: `git -C "$PWD" rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
    42	#                         falling back to MARATHON_HOME outside a git repo)
    43	#   MARATHON_DRIVE      — marathon-drive.sh path (default: <harness-home>/relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh)
    44	#   MARATHON_YAML_BIN   — bin/marathon-yaml path (default: <harness-home>/bin/marathon-yaml)
    45	#   TICK_BIN            — tick binary (default: <harness-home>/bin/tick)
    46	#   MARATHON_CLOSEOUT_BIN — marathon-closeout.sh path (default: <harness-home>/relay-automation/marathon-closeout.sh)
    47	#   MARATHON_ALLOW_PLAN_OUTSIDE_WORKING — 1 permits a --plan outside PROJECT/2-WORKING/ (GH-212)
    48	# Real runs also inherit the turn-taker env (CLAUDE_BIN, *_TURN_ROOT, …), passed straight through.
    49	#
    50	# Exit: 0 all phases approved · N the failing phase's marathon-drive exit code · 2 usage/parse error.
    51	
    52	HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    53	MARATHON_HOME="${MARATHON_HOME:-"$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"}"
    54	if [[ -n "${MARATHON_ROOT:-}" ]]; then
    55	  ROOT="$MARATHON_ROOT"
    56	elif ROOT="$(git -C "${PWD:-.}" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)"; then
    57	  :
    58	else
    59	  ROOT="$MARATHON_HOME"
    60	fi
    61	TICK_BIN="${TICK_BIN:-"$MARATHON_HOME/bin/tick"}"
    62	DRIVE_BIN="${MARATHON_DRIVE:-"$MARATHON_HOME/relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh"}"
    63	YAML_BIN="${MARATHON_YAML_BIN:-"$MARATHON_HOME/bin/marathon-yaml"}"
    64	CLOSEOUT_BIN="${MARATHON_CLOSEOUT_BIN:-"$MARATHON_HOME/relay-automation/marathon-closeout.sh"}"
    65	
    66	die() { printf 'marathon: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 2; }
    67	log() { printf 'marathon: %s\n' "$*"; }
    68	
    69	XYZ_APPEND_BIN="${XYZ_APPEND_BIN:-"$MARATHON_HOME/utils/telemetry/append-xyz-completion.sh"}"
    70	
    71	# GH-75: the ONE whole-run completion record for a marathon.sh-orchestrated run. Each per-phase
    72	# marathon-drive runs with XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT=marathon-phase (its own hook silent), so this is the
    73	# only place a marathon.sh run is recorded — on BOTH the success tail AND the halt path, so a failed
    74	# run isn't silently absent from XYZ.json (GH-75 review: an early halt used to skip the tail entirely,
    75	# emitting nothing — worse than a bare marathon-drive halt, which does emit red). Best-effort.
    76	xyz_marathon_run_emit() {  # <health> <description>
    77	  [[ -x "$XYZ_APPEND_BIN" ]] || return 0
    78	  local plan; plan="$(basename "$PLAN")"; plan="${plan%.*}"; [[ -n "$plan" ]] || plan="marathon"
    79	  "$XYZ_APPEND_BIN" marathon "$plan" "$1" "$plan" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    80	}
    81	
    82	usage() {
    83	  cat <<'EOF'
    84	Usage: marathon.sh --plan MARATHON.yaml [--builder A] [--phases-dir D] [--pre-advance-cmd C]
    85	                    [--dry-run] [--force] [--retry PHASE-ID] [--closeout-pr]
    86	
    87	  --plan PATH            MARATHON.yaml to run (required). Must resolve under PROJECT/2-WORKING/ in
    88	                          the target repo (GH-212) — exempt: paths under this harness's own home
    89	                          (shipped examples), or MARATHON_ALLOW_PLAN_OUTSIDE_WORKING=1.
    90	  --builder AGENT         Builder agent id (default: codex — no per-call API charge; bills via the
    91	                          Codex/ChatGPT subscription). --builder claude spawns a headless Claude
    92	                          Code CLI subprocess instead: a SEPARATE, PER-CALL API-BILLED turn-taker —
    93	                          an explicit, cost-acknowledged choice, not the default.
    94	  --phases-dir DIR        Where to create <dir>/<id>/ (default: <repo-root>/marathon-system).
    95	  --target-root DIR       Foreign git repo the BUILD lands in; forwarded to marathon-drive.sh (GH-11).
    96	                          The relay thread, tick token, marathon-system/ and relay-system/ transcripts all stay
    97	                          in THIS harness repo — only code changes land in DIR. Use this when the target
    98	                          repo cannot track harness output (e.g. a public repo that gitignores marathon-system/
    99	                          and relay-system/ on purpose): without it, marathon-drive's `git add` of
   100	                          RELAY.md / ESCALATION.md / the transcript fails and the phase HALTs.
   101	                          Plan and brief paths resolve against DIR when set.
   102	  --pre-advance-cmd CMD   Gate before phase.approved (default: bash validate.sh, per phase).
   103	  --dry-run               Render each phase's relay file and print the tick seed; exit without running.
   104	  --force                 GH-45: bypass the per-lane attempt cap for this run.
   105	  --retry PHASE-ID        GH-116: retry one phase with a fresh relay-task suffix.
   106	  --closeout-pr           Open (but never merge) a PR after a successful marathon. Closeout failure is logged
   107	                          and does not change the successful marathon exit code.
   108	EOF
   109	}
   110	
   111	PLAN=""; BUILDER="codex"; PHASES_DIR=""; PRE_ADVANCE_CMD=""; DRY_RUN=0; FORCE=0; RETRY_PHASE=""; CLOSEOUT_PR=0
   112	TARGET_ROOT=""   # GH-11 passthrough: foreign repo the BUILD lands in; relay/transcripts stay in ROOT
   113	while (($# > 0)); do
   114	  case "$1" in
   115	    --plan)            PLAN="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
   116	    --builder)         BUILDER="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
   117	    --phases-dir)      PHASES_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
   118	    --target-root)     TARGET_ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
   119	    --pre-advance-cmd) PRE_ADVANCE_CMD="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
   120	    --dry-run)         DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
   121	    --force)           FORCE=1; shift ;;   # GH-45: forward to each phase so a parked lane can be re-fired
   122	    --retry)           RETRY_PHASE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;   # GH-116: retry one phase with a fresh relay-task suffix
   123	    --closeout-pr)     CLOSEOUT_PR=1; shift ;;
   124	    --help)            usage; exit 0 ;;
   125	    *)                 die "unknown argument: $1" ;;
   126	  esac
   127	done
   128	[[ -n "$PLAN" ]] || { die "--plan MARATHON.yaml required"; }
   129	[[ -f "$PLAN" ]] || die "plan not found: $PLAN"
   130	
   131	# GH-212: plan-location guard. A marathon's plan artifacts (this YAML + its phase briefs) belong
   132	# under PROJECT/2-WORKING/<capture-doc>/, not a standalone top-level folder (e.g. marathon-plans/)
   133	# an agent might pattern-match from a prior repo. Exempt: paths under this harness's own home
   134	# (MARATHON_HOME) — shipped reference examples (e.g. MARATHON.example.yaml), not an agent-authored
   135	# plan for a target repo. Override for a legitimate non-default location:
   136	# MARATHON_ALLOW_PLAN_OUTSIDE_WORKING=1.
   137	_plan_abs="$(cd "$(dirname "$PLAN")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$PLAN")"
   138	# Canonicalize with `pwd -P` unconditionally (relative AND already-absolute input): ROOT can come
   139	# from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (symlink-resolved) or a raw MARATHON_ROOT env override
   140	# (whatever form the caller passed), so either side of this comparison can be a logical (non -P)
   141	# path — canonicalize both or a macOS /var -> /private/var checkout falsely flags every plan.
   142	# symlinks (e.g. macOS /var -> /private/var), so a logical (non -P) comparison here would falsely
   143	# flag every plan as "outside" on such a checkout (same pitfall swarm-preflight.sh works around).
   144	# On a --target-root run the plan lives in the TARGET repo's PROJECT/2-WORKING/, not the harness's,
   145	# so this guard must measure against that repo — otherwise every cross-repo plan falsely "resolves
   146	# outside PROJECT/2-WORKING/" and dies. GH-212's intent is unchanged: the plan must sit under
   147	# PROJECT/2-WORKING/ of whichever repo owns it.
   148	_plan_base="${TARGET_ROOT:-$ROOT}"
   149	_root_canon="$(cd "$_plan_base" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P || printf '%s' "$_plan_base")"
   150	_home_canon="$(cd "$MARATHON_HOME" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P || printf '%s' "$MARATHON_HOME")"
   151	_plan_rel_root="${_plan_abs#"$_root_canon"/}"
   152	case "$_plan_rel_root" in
   153	  PROJECT/2-WORKING/*) ;;   # in the expected home — proceed
   154	  *)
   155	    case "$_plan_abs" in
   156	      "$_home_canon"/*) ;;   # harness-owned reference material — exempt
   157	      *)
   158	        if [[ "${MARATHON_ALLOW_PLAN_OUTSIDE_WORKING:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
   159	          die "plan '$PLAN' resolves outside PROJECT/2-WORKING/ (got: $_plan_rel_root). Marathon plans (MARATHON.yaml + phase briefs) belong under PROJECT/2-WORKING/<capture-doc>/, not a standalone folder — see GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md Conventions. Override: MARATHON_ALLOW_PLAN_OUTSIDE_WORKING=1."
   160	        fi
   161	        log "MARATHON_ALLOW_PLAN_OUTSIDE_WORKING=1 — proceeding with a plan outside PROJECT/2-WORKING/ ($_plan_rel_root)"
   162	        ;;
   163	    esac
   164	    ;;
   165	esac
   166	
   167	# GH-484: default `marathon-system/`, matching `relay-system/`. This default is computed here
   168	# INDEPENDENTLY of the driver's own — marathon.sh forwards --phases-dir explicitly on every phase
   169	# (see the drive_args below), so the driver's default is never consulted on this path. Both must
   170	# agree or a marathon.sh run and a direct marathon-drive run would write to different places.
   171	PHASES_DIR="${PHASES_DIR:-"$ROOT/marathon-system"}"
   172	export TICK_REPO_ROOT="$ROOT"
   173	
   174	# Parse + validate + resolve order. A malformed/cyclic plan halts the whole run here (exit 2).
   175	PLAN_TSV="$("$YAML_BIN" "$PLAN")" || die "plan parse failed (see above)"
   176	[[ -n "$PLAN_TSV" ]] || die "plan has no phases"
   177	PLAN_NAME="$(sed -n 's/^name:[[:space:]]*//p' "$PLAN" | head -n1 | sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//')"
   178	phase_count="$(printf '%s\n' "$PLAN_TSV" | grep -c .)"
   179	log "plan: $PLAN — $phase_count phase(s) in execution order"
   180	
   181	idx=0
   182	# Read TSV with a NON-whitespace field separator (US / \037): `IFS=$'\t' read` coalesces consecutive
   183	# tabs (tab is whitespace-class), which would collapse empty columns and shift every field. Translate
   184	# tabs → \037 so empty fields (no rounds / no depends_on / no artifact / no turn_timeout_s) are
   185	# preserved positionally.
   186	while IFS=$'\037' read -r id reviewer rounds depends_on brief artifact turn_timeout_s name; do
   187	  [[ -n "$id" ]] || continue
   188	  idx=$((idx + 1))
   189	  rounds="${rounds:-2}"
   190	  cap=$((2 * rounds + 1))
   191	  lane_ns=""
   192	  [[ -n "$PLAN_NAME" ]] && lane_ns="${PLAN_NAME}--${id}"
   193	  [[ -n "$brief" ]] || die "phase $id: no 'brief:' in the plan — a phase needs a task to run"
   194	  # Briefs live beside the plan, so they resolve against the repo the plan came from. On a
   195	  # --target-root run that is the TARGET repo, not this harness — resolving against $ROOT would
   196	  # look for the target's briefs inside the harness clone and die "brief file not found".
   197	  brief_base="${TARGET_ROOT:-$ROOT}"
   198	  case "$brief" in /*) brief_path="$brief" ;; *) brief_path="$brief_base/$brief" ;; esac
   199	  [[ -f "$brief_path" ]] || die "phase $id: brief file not found: $brief_path"
   200	
   201	  log "── phase $idx/$phase_count: $id (reviewer=$reviewer, round-cap=$cap${artifact:+, artifact=$artifact}${turn_timeout_s:+, turn-timeout=${turn_timeout_s}s}) ──"
   202	
   203	  drive_args=( --phase-id "$id" --reviewer "$reviewer" --builder "$BUILDER"
   204	               --phase-brief "$brief_path" --round-cap "$cap" --phases-dir "$PHASES_DIR" )
   205	  [[ -n "$artifact" ]] && drive_args+=( --artifact "$artifact" )
   206	  [[ -n "$TARGET_ROOT" ]] && drive_args+=( --target-root "$TARGET_ROOT" )
   207	  [[ -n "$PRE_ADVANCE_CMD" ]] && drive_args+=( --pre-advance-cmd "$PRE_ADVANCE_CMD" )
   208	  ((FORCE)) && drive_args+=( --force )   # GH-45: bypass the per-lane attempt cap for this run
   209	  # GH-116: only the phase named by --retry gets a task-name override — every other phase still lets
   210	  # marathon-drive.sh derive its default MARATHON-<ID>-TURN name, unaffected.
   211	  if [[ -n "$RETRY_PHASE" && "$id" == "$RETRY_PHASE" ]]; then
   212	    id_upper="$(printf '%s' "$id" | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')"
   213	    retry_n=2
   214	    # First unused suffix, not a hardcoded -2: keep bumping while that task name already exists
   215	    # (tick info exits 0 once a task has any recorded state — spent or not, it's not reusable).
   216	    while "$TICK_BIN" info "MARATHON-${id_upper}-TURN-${retry_n}" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
   217	      retry_n=$((retry_n + 1))
   218	    done
   219	    retry_task="MARATHON-${id_upper}-TURN-${retry_n}"
   220	    log "phase $id: --retry requested — overriding relay task to $retry_task (first unused suffix)"
   221	    drive_args+=( --relay-task "$retry_task" )
   222	  fi
   223	  if ((DRY_RUN)); then drive_args+=( --dry-run ); fi
   224	
   225	  phase_exit=0
   226	  # GH-75: mark each per-phase marathon-drive call so its (and its nested relay-drive's) XYZ.json hook
   227	  # stays silent — this orchestrator emits a SINGLE harness:"marathon" whole-run record below, never
   228	  # one per phase.
   229	  if [[ -n "$turn_timeout_s" ]]; then
   230	    MARATHON_ROOT="$ROOT" MARATHON_LANE_NS="$lane_ns" TICK_BIN="$TICK_BIN" XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT=marathon-phase \
   231	      RELAY_TURN_TIMEOUT_S="$turn_timeout_s" \
   232	      bash "$DRIVE_BIN" "${drive_args[@]}" || phase_exit=$?
   233	  else
   234	    MARATHON_ROOT="$ROOT" MARATHON_LANE_NS="$lane_ns" TICK_BIN="$TICK_BIN" XYZ_HARNESS_CONTEXT=marathon-phase \
   235	      bash "$DRIVE_BIN" "${drive_args[@]}" || phase_exit=$?
   236	  fi
   237	  if [[ "$phase_exit" -ne 0 ]]; then
   238	    log "HALT: phase $id failed (marathon-drive exit $phase_exit) — chain stops; later phases NOT started"
   239	    case "$phase_exit" in
   240	      3) _halt_reason="relay no-progress" ;;
   241	      4) _halt_reason="relay cap/close-mismatch" ;;
   242	      5) _halt_reason="pre-advance gate failed" ;;
   243	      6) _halt_reason="containment violation" ;;
   244	      7) _halt_reason="turn timeout / hang" ;;
   245	      *) _halt_reason="marathon-drive exit $phase_exit" ;;
   246	    esac
   247	    xyz_marathon_run_emit red "halted at phase $idx of $phase_count ($id) — $_halt_reason"
   248	    exit "$phase_exit"
   249	  fi
   250	done < <(printf '%s\n' "$PLAN_TSV" | tr '\t' '\037')
   251	
   252	if ((DRY_RUN)); then
   253	  log "dry-run complete: $phase_count phase(s) would run in order"
   254	  exit 0
   255	fi
   256	
   257	if ((CLOSEOUT_PR)); then
   258	  closeout_plan="${PLAN_NAME:-$(basename "${PLAN%.*}")}"
   259	  closeout_event_dir="$ROOT/.tick/events"
   260	  closeout_event_count=0
   261	  closeout_event_types=""
   262	  if [[ -d "$closeout_event_dir" ]]; then
   263	    closeout_event_count="$(find "$closeout_event_dir" -type f -name '*.jsonl' -print | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   264	    closeout_event_types="$(find "$closeout_event_dir" -type f -name '*.jsonl' -print | LC_ALL=C sort | while IFS= read -r event_file; do
   265	      sed -n 's/.*"type":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$event_file"
   266	    done | LC_ALL=C sort -u | paste -sd, -)"
   267	  fi
   268	  closeout_notes="Marathon plan: $closeout_plan
   269	Phases approved: $phase_count/$phase_count
   270	Tick events: $closeout_event_count${closeout_event_types:+ ($closeout_event_types)}"
   271	  if ! bash "$CLOSEOUT_BIN" --repo "$ROOT" --open-only --title "Marathon: $closeout_plan" --notes "$closeout_notes"; then
   272	    log "closeout PR failed after successful marathon; leaving marathon successful"
   273	  fi
   274	fi
   275	"$TICK_BIN" log marathon.complete "MARATHON-RUN" --agent marathon > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
   276	
   277	# GH-75: the whole-run success record (title/sessionId = plan name, "N of M phase(s) approved").
   278	xyz_marathon_run_emit green "$phase_count of $phase_count phase(s) approved"
   279	
   280	log "marathon complete — all $phase_count phase(s) approved"
   281	exit 0
     1	# XYZ — Multi-Agent Coordination Beta
     2	
     3	**XYZ lets several AI coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, and agy (Google's Antigravity CLI) — work
     4	on the same repo at the same time without overwriting each other's work.**
     5	
     6	## What XYZ is
     7	
     8	It's built in two layers:
     9	
    10	- **`tick`** — the kernel: a tiny local event-log CLI that hands out collision-free, path-scoped
    11	  work claims, so two agents never edit the same thing at once. No server, no API keys, no remote.
    12	- **`relay-automation/`** — the product on top of `tick`: it runs agents in **turns** (one builds,
    13	  another reviews) headlessly, so you can hand a task to Codex or agy and let them iterate toward
    14	  done without babysitting the handoff.
    15	
    16	It's a working beta, not a polished product — but the kernel is test-covered and the relay stack
    17	is the main active surface.
    18	
    19	## Quickstart — prove it works (no accounts needed)
    20	
    21	Requires **Node 18+** and **git** (the `tick` kernel runs on Node). No accounts or API keys.
    22	
    23	```bash
    24	npm install
    25	./validate.sh
    26	```
    27	
    28	(`npm install` pulls the two parser dependencies the test suite needs — skip it and the
    29	suite stops at `Cannot find module 'acorn'`.)
    30	
    31	That runs the full kernel + coordination test suite, with **no accounts or API keys required** —
    32	the fastest proof the coordination kernel actually works. It's the whole suite, not a smoke test,
    33	so **budget 5–10 minutes** on a first run. The suite prints its own pass count at the end; if it's
    34	green, you're good.
    35	
    36	> **⚠️ Run this un-sandboxed.** Under Claude Code's default Bash sandbox — or any sandboxed agent
    37	> harness — this command prints **nothing for several minutes** before failing, because the suite's
    38	> `mktemp -d` scratch directories are blocked. It looks like a hang, not a permissions error, and
    39	> it is this repo's single most common false alarm. Turn the sandbox off for this command
    40	> (`/sandbox` in Claude Code, or run it yourself in a normal terminal) before concluding anything
    41	> is broken.
    42	
    43	## Then pick your path
    44	
    45	- **New here for the beta test?** → start at [Beta Tester Onboarding](#beta-tester-onboarding) below.
    46	- **Run a live relay** — hand a real task to Codex/agy and let them build→review it →
    47	  start at **[relay-automation/README.md](relay-automation/README.md)**. Live turns need each CLI
    48	  installed and authenticated first: see
    49	  **[Set up Codex, agy, and Pi](relay-automation/README.md#set-up-codex-agy-and-pi-headless-bring-up)**.
    50	  For phase/status context, the project hub is
    51	  [PROJECT/4-MISC/AUTOMATED-RELAY.md](PROJECT/4-MISC/AUTOMATED-RELAY.md).
    52	- **Here for the kernel** — how the `tick` coordination primitive works →
    53	  read [What `tick` is](#what-tick-is), then the source in [bin/tick](bin/tick), [src/](src), [test/](test).
    54	- **Install `tick` into another repo** → see [Install into another repo](#install-into-another-repo).
    55	
    56	> **Editing this repo as an agent?** Read [ROUTER.md](ROUTER.md) for the startup order and canonical
    57	> entry points. It's the map for *working on* the repo, not for *using* it — a human landing here
    58	> should start with the Quickstart above.
    59	
    60	---
    61	
    62	> **⏳ Beta-testing period:** the onboarding guide below runs for the duration of the beta. Once the
    63	> beta wraps, this section moves out and the README continues straight from
    64	> [What XYZ is](#what-xyz-is) above. Discussion: [issue #123](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/123).
    65	
    66	## Beta Tester Onboarding
    67	
    68	**TL;DR:** You can get immediate value from **Relay** and **Consult** with just this XYZ repo — no
    69	PDDA required. PDDA installation is only needed if you want the full eventual automation path
    70	(**Swarm** and especially **Marathon**). Start with the fast path, graduate to PDDA later if you
    71	like what you see.
    72	
    73	Background links (not required for this test):
    74	
    75	- GiantBrains Claude Skills — https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/giant-brains-claude-skills
    76	- PDDA (the doc-governance half of the system) — https://github.com/Hypercart-Dev-Tools/pdda
    77	
    78	### The four modes of operation
    79	
    80	XYZ has four modes. They stack — each one builds on the trust you develop with the previous:
    81	
    82	1. **Consult** — a one-shot, parallel second opinion. The same question fans out to Codex and agy
    83	   at the same time, each answers independently in an isolated copy of the repo, and the answers
    84	   are reconciled into one. Nothing is modified; it's purely advisory. Lowest risk, fastest payoff.
    85	2. **Relay** — an iterative, turn-based loop between two agents on one shared file: a **Producer**
    86	   builds an artifact, a **Reviewer** critiques and proposes fixes, and they hand off back and
    87	   forth until the artifact converges. This replaces you copy-pasting output between two agent
    88	   windows. Changes are confined to the relay thread file and the artifact under review.
    89	3. **Swarm** — two or more agents working **concurrently** on the same repo, each claiming a
    90	   non-overlapping, path-scoped lane (via the `tick` kernel) so they never collide. Good for
    91	   parallel builds or parallel codebase recon. This is where PDDA's doc structure starts to matter,
    92	   because lanes are carved from well-defined task docs.
    93	4. **Marathon** — the full automation payoff: a queue of pre-flighted tasks (built up during the
    94	   day) fired as one long autonomous run, typically end-of-day or overnight. Marathon **requires**
    95	   PDDA, because the preflight scripts rely on PDDA's opinionated docs/roadmap structure to verify
    96	   every queued task is well-specified before anything runs unattended.
    97	
    98	How they fit together: **Consult** answers "what do the other models think?", **Relay** answers
    99	"build this and have it reviewed until it's right", **Swarm** answers "do several independent
   100	things at once", and **Marathon** answers "do all of today's queued work while I sleep." Consult
   101	and Relay need only this XYZ repo. Swarm and Marathon are where PDDA earns its setup cost.
   102	
   103	### Before you start — safety and reversibility
   104	
   105	Everything below is designed to be reversible, but please help it along:
   106	
   107	- **Create a fresh branch (or git worktree) in *both* repos you touch** — one in your clone of
   108	  XYZ, and one in each target project where you'll run relays or install PDDA. E.g.
   109	  `git checkout -b xyz-beta-test`. If anything goes sideways, recovery is just
   110	  `git checkout main` and deleting the branch. If you use `git worktree` directly, read
   111	  [WORKTREE-SAFETY.md](WORKTREE-SAFETY.md) first — a couple of its operations (force-removing a
   112	  worktree directory, moving/relinking one) leave stale git metadata if done by hand instead of
   113	  through `git worktree remove`/`repair`.
   114	- **What each step actually touches** (so you know how to undo it):
   115	  - *Skill install* — symlinks skill folders into `~/.claude/skills/` (user-level). A `git pull` in your XYZ clone will silently update your installed skills. Undo: delete those symlinks. Your repos are untouched.
   116	  - *Relay runs* — write a dated thread file under `relay-system/<date>/` plus the artifact being
   117	    reviewed, on your branch. Undo: discard the branch.
   118	  - *Consult runs* — advisory only; agents work in isolated copies. Nothing to undo. **Known
   119	    limitation:** the `agy` CLI has been observed grounding its answers against the real repo
   120	    instead of confining itself to its isolated copy, undermining the "isolated" guarantee for that
   121	    one advisor specifically. A detect-and-fail check now catches this case and hard-fails the turn
   122	    rather than silently returning a contaminated answer, though it isn't a complete fix yet — see
   123	    [#178](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/178) and
   124	    [#183](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/183).
   125	  - *PDDA install* — adds scripts and an opinionated `PROJECT/` docs structure to the target repo.
   126	    Undo: it's all ordinary tracked files on your branch, so discarding the branch fully reverts it.
   127	- Clone this XYZ repo locally. Clone PDDA **only** if you're going for the full automation path.
   128	
   129	### Prerequisites — install and authenticate these before the fast path
   130	
   131	The fast path below shells out to the Codex and agy CLIs. **Install and sign in to both before you
   132	start** — a relay or consult fails mid-run, not at startup, if either isn't logged in.
   133	
   134	| Prerequisite | Install | Notes |
   135	|---|---|---|
   136	| **Codex CLI** (OpenAI) | <https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-codex-app/> | Authenticate with your ChatGPT account. |
   137	| **agy CLI** (Google Antigravity — the **CLI**, not just the desktop app) | <https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli> | Authenticate through the Antigravity desktop app. You can hand this URL to Claude Code and ask it to install for you. |
   138	| **Node 18+ and git** | your usual package manager | Needed by the `tick` kernel and the Quickstart above. |
   139	| **Python 3.8+** | usually already present | See the runtime note below. |
   140	
   141	Full per-CLI verification steps, environment variables, and troubleshooting live in
   142	**[Set up Codex, agy, and Pi](relay-automation/README.md#set-up-codex-agy-and-pi-headless-bring-up)**.
   143	
   144	- **Runtime — Python by default.** The harness entry points run their **Python** implementation by
   145	  default. Every shim keeps its original Bash body inline as the escape hatch, so you can force the
   146	  legacy Bash path at any granularity: one command with `XYZ_PYTHON=0 <command>`, a whole session or
   147	  CI job with `export XYZ_PYTHON=0`, or permanently with `git revert <flip-sha>` (the flip is one
   148	  isolated commit). Python 3.8+ is required; if `python3` is missing or too old a shim prints a warning
   149	  and falls back to Bash on its own.
   150	- **Supply-chain note (agy):** The `agy` CLI performs background self-updates. This interacts oddly with the pin-to-audited-commit discipline used for most headless tools, as your underlying agent model may update mid-project.
   151	- **Agent users: run un-sandboxed.** If you're driving this from Claude Code (or another sandboxed
   152	  agent harness), relay and consult runs need real keychain access and outbound network egress to
   153	  reach Codex/agy — a sandboxed shell will fail with "Operation not permitted" or a blocked-host
   154	  error that looks like a bug but is really the sandbox. Disable the sandbox for these commands
   155	  before concluding something is broken.
   156	
   157	### Fast path: immediate value, no PDDA
   158	
   159	1. Create a working branch in your XYZ clone.
   160	2. In the XYZ repo, ask Claude Code to: *"install the /relay-xyz and /consult skills for me
   161	   system-wide."*
   162	3. In any target project (on its own fresh branch), you can now:
   163	   - Run a **Consult** for a cross-model second opinion on a design, doc, or decision.
   164	   - Run a **Relay** to have a Producer/Reviewer pair converge a real artifact.
   165	
   166	No PDDA compliance is enforced on the target project for either of these. This is the recommended
   167	starting point for all beta testers.
   168	
   169	### Full automation path: PDDA + Swarm/Marathon
   170	
   171	Only take this path once the fast path works for you and you want unattended, queued execution:
   172	
   173	1. In the target project repo, **create a new branch first**, then run PDDA's `install.sh`.
   174	2. Ask Claude Code to help make the project's docs folder structure PDDA-compliant so XYZ can
   175	   operate on it cleanly. (PDDA ships auto-triage scripts that do most of this restructuring for
   176	   you.)
   177	3. Ask Claude Code to create a **Marathon Plan** file, and add tasks to it throughout the day as
   178	   they come up.
   179	4. Near end of day, ask Claude Code to run the **preflight scripts** — these check your docs and
   180	   GitHub issues for Marathon/Swarm viability so nothing under-specified runs unattended.
   181	5. When preflight is green, ask Claude Code to **fire the Marathon**.
   182	
   183	### Important note on PDDA's structure
   184	
   185	PDDA's folder structure is deliberately opinionated. That setup cost is the trade for what
   186	Marathon gives you: because every task lives in a predictable doc structure, the system can
   187	preflight, queue, and execute a full day's work without you babysitting it. If that trade doesn't
   188	appeal yet, stay on the fast path — Relay and Consult deliver value on day one with zero
   189	restructuring.
   190
