   192	
   193	## Glossary — the four terms you'll hit first
   194	
   195	(For how the operating modes — Consult, Relay, Swarm, Marathon — relate to each other, see
   196	[The four modes of operation](#the-four-modes-of-operation) in the beta section above.)
   197	
   198	- **`tick`** — the coordination kernel: a shared local event log (`.tick/events/`) that agents
   199	  claim work through, serialized by an `O_EXCL` lock.
   200	- **relay** — a turn-based loop where one agent builds and another reviews, handing off through
   201	  files instead of a human copy-pasting between windows.
   202	- **Marathon** (`relay-automation/marathon.sh`) — chains several relay build→review phases from a
   203	  `MARATHON.yaml`, in `depends_on` order. The multi-agent coordinator built on the relay loop.
   204	- **agy** — the Antigravity CLI (Google), one of the agents XYZ coordinates alongside Claude Code
   205	  and Codex.
   206	
   207	## FAQ
   208	
   209	### Is XYZ a "graph" — does it do graph engineering?
   210	
   211	Partly, and the parts it leaves out are deliberate. If you arrive with the standard agent-graph
   212	vocabulary (a DAG of nodes and edges, parallel stages, routing decisions), the Glossary entry above
   213	will read as more than it says. The precise answer:
   214	
   215	**What matches.** Phases are real nodes — each gets `marathon-system/<id>/RELAY.md`, a tick token, a
   216	reviewer, a brief, and an artifact allowlist, with an LLM turn as the body. Inside a phase there is
   217	a genuine LLM-selected edge: the reviewer writes `STATUS:`, and `utils/py/relay_drive.py` treats
   218	`Approved`/`Closed` as terminal and anything else as another round, bounded by a round cap. Every
   219	phase boundary runs a verification gate, which must be able to *start* before turn 1 — a missing
   220	gate fails fast rather than being skipped. And the whole run is an inspectable state machine
   221	(`.tick/events/`, `RELAY.md`, `ESCALATION.md` with typed reason codes) rather than a model's
   222	self-report.
   223	
   224	**What doesn't.** There is no DAG. `depends_on` is scalar-only — one dependency per phase — so a
   225	join is inexpressible: "p4 after p2 *and* p3" cannot be written. There is no parallel execution;
   226	`relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml` states that phases run strictly one at a time and that a
   227	disjoint write-set does not buy you parallelism. `depends_on` **validates** the order you authored
   228	rather than **deriving** one, which inverts the usual graph model. And a failure halts the chain —
   229	there is no conditional edge to a remediation node.
   230	
   231	So: a sequential chain of agent-driven build→review loops, with hard gates at every boundary. The
   232	scheduling a graph engine exists to automate is handed to the operator on purpose — see
   233	`GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md` §8, and `utils/swarm-preflight.sh`, which is the *producer* of a run packet
   234	and never its executor.
   235	
   236	Parallelism does exist, but as **swarms**: separate agents in separate worktrees or clones on
   237	disjoint write-sets, coordinated by `tick` locks. That is arranged by the operator, not scheduled
   238	from a dependency graph.
   239	
   240	### Do phases run in parallel? What does `depends_on` actually do?
   241	
   242	No, and less than you'd think. Phases run **one at a time**, in the order they appear in the plan.
   243	A phase *without* `depends_on` is not "unordered" or "parallel-safe" — it simply runs when its turn
   244	comes. `depends_on` constrains that order; it does not create it.
   245	
   246	It also takes exactly one phase id, unquoted (`depends_on: p3`). The list form `depends_on: [p3]`
   247	parses as the literal string and aborts the plan with an unknown-phase error that points at your
   248	phase ids rather than at the field's shape. Chain them (`p3 → p4 → p5`) to express a longer order.
   249	
   250	Analysing your phases for a disjoint write-set is still worth doing — it is how you learn which
   251	phases genuinely need `depends_on` — but it will not make them concurrent.
   252	
   253	Always `--dry-run` a new plan first. It parses every field and prints the real execution order at
   254	zero cost, which is the cheapest way to catch both a mis-shaped field and a wrong mental model.
   255	
   256	## Repo map
   257	
   258	- `relay-automation/` — scripts and operator docs for poll-driven relays, watchdogs, headless turn-takers, and consult.
   259	- `skills/` — packaged skill surfaces, including `relay-xyz`, `relay-automation`, `xyz`, consult helpers, and
   260	  [`ponytail`](skills/ponytail/SKILL.md) (the `/ponytail` lens definition cited throughout
   261	  `PROJECT/` docs and PDDA's `/idea` Phase 0 — see [GH-180](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/180)).
   262	  Claude Code only scans `~/.claude/skills/`, so a fresh clone won't see these until you symlink them in —
   263	  run `bash skills/relay-xyz/install.sh` once per clone/machine to make the `/relay-xyz` skill discoverable
   264	  (see [skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md](skills/relay-xyz/SKILL.md#first-time-setup-on-a-new-clone-or-machine-make-the-skill-discoverable)).
   265	- `skills/marathon-triage/`, `skills/marathon-cleanup/`, `skills/10days/` — the marathon operator
   266	  skills: triage PDDA intake + active work into a ranked, preflight-checked, collision-safe queue
   267	  ([`marathon-triage`](skills/marathon-triage/SKILL.md)); archive only lanes with verified completion
   268	  evidence after a run ([`marathon-cleanup`](skills/marathon-cleanup/SKILL.md)); and — the one deliberate,
   269	  operator-authorized auto-fire exception to the "ask before firing" rule — sweep recent GitHub issues into
   270	  a marathon and execute it unattended ([`10days`](skills/10days/SKILL.md)). See [GH-240](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/240).
   271	- `skills/file-xyz-bug/` — file a harness bug from **any other repo** into this repo's `PROJECT/1-INBOX/`
   272	  (GH issue + capture doc + ROADMAP park), without touching the repo you're standing in.
   273	- `relay-system/` — relay transcripts, reviews, and dogfood runs.
   274	- `PROJECT/2-WORKING/` — active project docs and working plans.
   275	- `bin/tick`, `src/`, `test/` — the `tick` coordination kernel and its test suite.
   276	- `utils/swarm-preflight.sh` — marathon intake planner: turns a project doc or a GH-issue bundle into a marathon-ready run packet (freshness + fix-still-required checks, readiness gate, Codex/agy lane plan). Run `utils/swarm-preflight.sh --help`; see [GH-25-SWARM-PREFLIGHT-PLANNER.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-25-SWARM-PREFLIGHT-PLANNER.md).
   277	- `utils/marathon-plan.sh` — the marathon planner/ranker: scores the whole ROADMAP ledger into waves of disjoint, collision-safe write-sets, and with `--deep` delegates to `swarm-preflight.sh --dry-run` per item for an authoritative freshness verdict. Writes `PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-<date>.md` — the "marathon file" the operator skills act on.
   278	- `utils/swe-diagram/` — dependency-free architecture/Git-history diagram generator; `layout: "git-lanes"` renders stacked branch lanes with commits left-to-right, driven by a local ref-reading generator that emits an auditable JSON spec plus self-contained HTML. See [GH-201](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/201).
   279	- `utils/git-bundle-snapshot.sh` + `relay-automation/hooks/gh177-sandbox-test-guard.sh` — the wipe-prevention layer: rotated `git bundle --all` backups on a daily cron, plus a PreToolUse hook that blocks running the test suite under a *sandboxed* Claude Code Bash call (the ignition for the GH-177 repo wipes). See [GH-233](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/233).
   280	- `install.sh` — materializes the `tick` runtime (`bin/tick` + `src/*.js`) into an external repo and records the install in a per-user, machine-local registry (`~/.config/xyz/registry.tsv`). See "Install into another repo" below.
   281	- `utils/hq/` — **HQ**, the multi-repo command center (`hq.sh` + `hq-lib.sh`); driven by the user-level `/hq` skill in `skills/hq/`. See [HQ — multi-repo command center](#hq--multi-repo-command-center) below.

     1	# XYZ — Multi-Agent Coordination Beta
     2	
     3	**XYZ lets several AI coding agents — Claude Code, Codex, and agy (Google's Antigravity CLI) — work
     4	on the same repo at the same time without overwriting each other's work.**
     5	
     6	## What XYZ is
     7	
     8	It's built in two layers:
     9	
    10	- **`tick`** — the kernel: a tiny local event-log CLI that hands out collision-free, path-scoped
    11	  work claims, so two agents never edit the same thing at once. No server, no API keys, no remote.
    12	- **`relay-automation/`** — the product on top of `tick`: it runs agents in **turns** (one builds,
    13	  another reviews) headlessly, so you can hand a task to Codex or agy and let them iterate toward
    14	  done without babysitting the handoff.
    15	
    16	It's a working beta, not a polished product — but the kernel is test-covered and the relay stack
    17	is the main active surface.
    18	
    19	## Quickstart — prove it works (no accounts needed)
    20	
    21	Requires **Node 18+** and **git** (the `tick` kernel runs on Node). No accounts or API keys.
    22	
    23	```bash
    24	npm install
    25	./validate.sh
    26	```
    27	
    28	(`npm install` pulls the two parser dependencies the test suite needs — skip it and the
    29	suite stops at `Cannot find module 'acorn'`.)
    30	
    31	That runs the full kernel + coordination test suite, with **no accounts or API keys required** —
    32	the fastest proof the coordination kernel actually works. It's the whole suite, not a smoke test,
    33	so **budget 5–10 minutes** on a first run. The suite prints its own pass count at the end; if it's
    34	green, you're good.
    35	
    36	> **⚠️ Run this un-sandboxed.** Under Claude Code's default Bash sandbox — or any sandboxed agent
    37	> harness — this command prints **nothing for several minutes** before failing, because the suite's
    38	> `mktemp -d` scratch directories are blocked. It looks like a hang, not a permissions error, and
    39	> it is this repo's single most common false alarm. Turn the sandbox off for this command
    40	> (`/sandbox` in Claude Code, or run it yourself in a normal terminal) before concluding anything
    41	> is broken.

    65	
    66	## Beta Tester Onboarding
    67	
    68	**TL;DR:** You can get immediate value from **Relay** and **Consult** with just this XYZ repo — no
    69	PDDA required. PDDA installation is only needed if you want the full eventual automation path
    70	(**Swarm** and especially **Marathon**). Start with the fast path, graduate to PDDA later if you
    71	like what you see.
    72	
    73	Background links (not required for this test):
    74	
    75	- GiantBrains Claude Skills — https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/giant-brains-claude-skills
    76	- PDDA (the doc-governance half of the system) — https://github.com/Hypercart-Dev-Tools/pdda
    77	
    78	### The four modes of operation
    79	
    80	XYZ has four modes. They stack — each one builds on the trust you develop with the previous:
    81	
    82	1. **Consult** — a one-shot, parallel second opinion. The same question fans out to Codex and agy
    83	   at the same time, each answers independently in an isolated copy of the repo, and the answers
    84	   are reconciled into one. Nothing is modified; it's purely advisory. Lowest risk, fastest payoff.
    85	2. **Relay** — an iterative, turn-based loop between two agents on one shared file: a **Producer**
    86	   builds an artifact, a **Reviewer** critiques and proposes fixes, and they hand off back and
    87	   forth until the artifact converges. This replaces you copy-pasting output between two agent
    88	   windows. Changes are confined to the relay thread file and the artifact under review.
    89	3. **Swarm** — two or more agents working **concurrently** on the same repo, each claiming a
    90	   non-overlapping, path-scoped lane (via the `tick` kernel) so they never collide. Good for
    91	   parallel builds or parallel codebase recon. This is where PDDA's doc structure starts to matter,
    92	   because lanes are carved from well-defined task docs.
    93	4. **Marathon** — the full automation payoff: a queue of pre-flighted tasks (built up during the
    94	   day) fired as one long autonomous run, typically end-of-day or overnight. Marathon **requires**
    95	   PDDA, because the preflight scripts rely on PDDA's opinionated docs/roadmap structure to verify
    96	   every queued task is well-specified before anything runs unattended.
    97	
    98	How they fit together: **Consult** answers "what do the other models think?", **Relay** answers
    99	"build this and have it reviewed until it's right", **Swarm** answers "do several independent
   100	things at once", and **Marathon** answers "do all of today's queued work while I sleep." Consult
   101	and Relay need only this XYZ repo. Swarm and Marathon are where PDDA earns its setup cost.
   102	
   103	### Before you start — safety and reversibility
   104	
   105	Everything below is designed to be reversible, but please help it along:
   106	
   107	- **Create a fresh branch (or git worktree) in *both* repos you touch** — one in your clone of
   108	  XYZ, and one in each target project where you'll run relays or install PDDA. E.g.
   109	  `git checkout -b xyz-beta-test`. If anything goes sideways, recovery is just
   110	  `git checkout main` and deleting the branch. If you use `git worktree` directly, read
   111	  [WORKTREE-SAFETY.md](WORKTREE-SAFETY.md) first — a couple of its operations (force-removing a
   112	  worktree directory, moving/relinking one) leave stale git metadata if done by hand instead of
   113	  through `git worktree remove`/`repair`.
   114	- **What each step actually touches** (so you know how to undo it):
   115	  - *Skill install* — symlinks skill folders into `~/.claude/skills/` (user-level). A `git pull` in your XYZ clone will silently update your installed skills. Undo: delete those symlinks. Your repos are untouched.
   116	  - *Relay runs* — write a dated thread file under `relay-system/<date>/` plus the artifact being
   117	    reviewed, on your branch. Undo: discard the branch.
   118	  - *Consult runs* — advisory only; agents work in isolated copies. Nothing to undo. **Known
   119	    limitation:** the `agy` CLI has been observed grounding its answers against the real repo
   120	    instead of confining itself to its isolated copy, undermining the "isolated" guarantee for that
   121	    one advisor specifically. A detect-and-fail check now catches this case and hard-fails the turn
   122	    rather than silently returning a contaminated answer, though it isn't a complete fix yet — see
   123	    [#178](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/178) and
   124	    [#183](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/183).
   125	  - *PDDA install* — adds scripts and an opinionated `PROJECT/` docs structure to the target repo.
   126	    Undo: it's all ordinary tracked files on your branch, so discarding the branch fully reverts it.
   127	- Clone this XYZ repo locally. Clone PDDA **only** if you're going for the full automation path.
   128	
   129	### Prerequisites — install and authenticate these before the fast path
   130	
   131	The fast path below shells out to the Codex and agy CLIs. **Install and sign in to both before you
   132	start** — a relay or consult fails mid-run, not at startup, if either isn't logged in.
   133	
   134	| Prerequisite | Install | Notes |
   135	|---|---|---|
   136	| **Codex CLI** (OpenAI) | <https://openai.com/index/introducing-the-codex-app/> | Authenticate with your ChatGPT account. |
   137	| **agy CLI** (Google Antigravity — the **CLI**, not just the desktop app) | <https://antigravity.google/product/antigravity-cli> | Authenticate through the Antigravity desktop app. You can hand this URL to Claude Code and ask it to install for you. |
   138	| **Node 18+ and git** | your usual package manager | Needed by the `tick` kernel and the Quickstart above. |
   139	| **Python 3.8+** | usually already present | See the runtime note below. |
   140	
   141	Full per-CLI verification steps, environment variables, and troubleshooting live in
   142	**[Set up Codex, agy, and Pi](relay-automation/README.md#set-up-codex-agy-and-pi-headless-bring-up)**.
   143	
   144	- **Runtime — Python by default.** The harness entry points run their **Python** implementation by
   145	  default. Every shim keeps its original Bash body inline as the escape hatch, so you can force the
   146	  legacy Bash path at any granularity: one command with `XYZ_PYTHON=0 <command>`, a whole session or
   147	  CI job with `export XYZ_PYTHON=0`, or permanently with `git revert <flip-sha>` (the flip is one
   148	  isolated commit). Python 3.8+ is required; if `python3` is missing or too old a shim prints a warning
   149	  and falls back to Bash on its own.
   150	- **Supply-chain note (agy):** The `agy` CLI performs background self-updates. This interacts oddly with the pin-to-audited-commit discipline used for most headless tools, as your underlying agent model may update mid-project.
   151	- **Agent users: run un-sandboxed.** If you're driving this from Claude Code (or another sandboxed
   152	  agent harness), relay and consult runs need real keychain access and outbound network egress to
   153	  reach Codex/agy — a sandboxed shell will fail with "Operation not permitted" or a blocked-host
   154	  error that looks like a bug but is really the sandbox. Disable the sandbox for these commands
   155	  before concluding something is broken.
   156	
   157	### Fast path: immediate value, no PDDA
   158	
   159	1. Create a working branch in your XYZ clone.
   160	2. In the XYZ repo, ask Claude Code to: *"install the /relay-xyz and /consult skills for me
   161	   system-wide."*
   162	3. In any target project (on its own fresh branch), you can now:
   163	   - Run a **Consult** for a cross-model second opinion on a design, doc, or decision.
   164	   - Run a **Relay** to have a Producer/Reviewer pair converge a real artifact.
   165	
   166	No PDDA compliance is enforced on the target project for either of these. This is the recommended
   167	starting point for all beta testers.
   168	
   169	### Full automation path: PDDA + Swarm/Marathon
   170	
   171	Only take this path once the fast path works for you and you want unattended, queued execution:
   172	
   173	1. In the target project repo, **create a new branch first**, then run PDDA's `install.sh`.
   174	2. Ask Claude Code to help make the project's docs folder structure PDDA-compliant so XYZ can
   175	   operate on it cleanly. (PDDA ships auto-triage scripts that do most of this restructuring for
   176	   you.)
   177	3. Ask Claude Code to create a **Marathon Plan** file, and add tasks to it throughout the day as
   178	   they come up.
   179	4. Near end of day, ask Claude Code to run the **preflight scripts** — these check your docs and
   180	   GitHub issues for Marathon/Swarm viability so nothing under-specified runs unattended.
   181	5. When preflight is green, ask Claude Code to **fire the Marathon**.
   182	
   183	### Important note on PDDA's structure
   184	
   185	PDDA's folder structure is deliberately opinionated. That setup cost is the trade for what
   186	Marathon gives you: because every task lives in a predictable doc structure, the system can
   187	preflight, queue, and execute a full day's work without you babysitting it. If that trade doesn't
   188	appeal yet, stay on the fast path — Relay and Consult deliver value on day one with zero
   189	restructuring.
   190	
   191	---
   192	
   193	## Glossary — the four terms you'll hit first
   194	
   195	(For how the operating modes — Consult, Relay, Swarm, Marathon — relate to each other, see
   196	[The four modes of operation](#the-four-modes-of-operation) in the beta section above.)
   197	
   198	- **`tick`** — the coordination kernel: a shared local event log (`.tick/events/`) that agents
   199	  claim work through, serialized by an `O_EXCL` lock.
   200	- **relay** — a turn-based loop where one agent builds and another reviews, handing off through
   201	  files instead of a human copy-pasting between windows.
   202	- **Marathon** (`relay-automation/marathon.sh`) — chains several relay build→review phases from a
   203	  `MARATHON.yaml`, in `depends_on` order. The multi-agent coordinator built on the relay loop.
   204	- **agy** — the Antigravity CLI (Google), one of the agents XYZ coordinates alongside Claude Code
   205	  and Codex.
   206	
   207	## FAQ
   208	
   209	### Is XYZ a "graph" — does it do graph engineering?
   210

README.md-224-**What doesn't.** There is no DAG. `depends_on` is scalar-only — one dependency per phase — so a
README.md:225:join is inexpressible: "p4 after p2 *and* p3" cannot be written. There is no parallel execution;
README.md-226-`relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml` states that phases run strictly one at a time and that a
README.md:227:disjoint write-set does not buy you parallelism. `depends_on` **validates** the order you authored
README.md-228-rather than **deriving** one, which inverts the usual graph model. And a failure halts the chain —
README.md-229-there is no conditional edge to a remediation node.

README.md:240:### Do phases run in parallel? What does `depends_on` actually do?
README.md-241-
README.md-242-No, and less than you'd think. Phases run **one at a time**, in the order they appear in the plan.
README.md:243:A phase *without* `depends_on` is not "unordered" or "parallel-safe" — it simply runs when its turn
README.md-244-comes. `depends_on` constrains that order; it does not create it.

PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-209-MARATHON-ROOT-LEAK-AUDIT.md-38-| What was just completed | What's next |
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-209-MARATHON-ROOT-LEAK-AUDIT.md-39-|---|---|
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-209-MARATHON-ROOT-LEAK-AUDIT.md:40:| Capture written; scope explicitly narrowed after finding the full architectural fix is not safely automatable (see Decision). Confirmed with operator via the marathon-scope selection. **New live evidence for the Problem, found running today's own marathon (2026-07-16):** phase `gh213`'s pre-advance gate command (`bash test/find-harness.sh && bash test/marathon.sh && ...`) ran nested INSIDE the still-live outer `marathon-drive.sh` process, and `test/marathon.sh`'s GH-205 resume sub-case failed there (`grep: .../phases/gh205/RELAY.md: No such file or directory`) despite passing 33/33 standalone immediately before and after. Confirmed by reproduction attempts with matching env vars (`TICK_REPO_ROOT`, `MARATHON_ROOT`, `MARATHON_BUILDER`/`REVIEWER`, `CODEX_AGENT`/`AGY_AGENT`, `RELAY_DRIVER_LOCKED=1`) that this specific set does NOT reproduce it standalone — the exact leak vector is still unidentified, but the phenomenon (nesting `test/marathon.sh`/`test/marathon-drive.sh` inside a live `marathon-drive.sh` process is unreliable) is now directly demonstrated, not just inferred from the original incident. Worked around today by not nesting those two test files in the marathon's own `--pre-advance-cmd` (verified standalone by the orchestrator instead). **The exact leak vector was found and fixed by this very phase's builder turn**: `MARATHON_LANE_NS` (set by the outer `marathon.sh`/`marathon-drive.sh` for the live phase) was leaking into `test/marathon.sh`/`test/marathon-drive.sh`'s own nested invocations of the real scripts, redirecting rendered relay paths under the outer phase's namespaced directory and breaking pre-existing path assertions — fixed with `unset MARATHON_LANE_NS` at the top of both test files (GH-207's own explicit namespaced test cases still set it per-invocation and remain covered). New `test/marathon-root-audit.sh` (13/13, registered in `validate.sh`) statically audits that every real-script invocation in the test suite is `MARATHON_ROOT`-scoped or fixture-local, going forward. Reviewed and Approved by agy (tick token confirmed `status: done`), but agy-turn.sh's isolation-breach detector then failed the TURN on a known false positive (GH-183, already tracked, unfixed) — the relay file's Approved content was committed by hand after independently re-verifying `test/marathon-root-audit.sh` (13/13), `test/marathon.sh` (33/33), `test/marathon-drive.sh` (85/85), and full `validate.sh` (green except the pre-existing #208). | Done. Continuing to `gh203`. |

PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md-20-
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md-21-## Goal
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md:22:Prevent a concurrent relay or marathon session from destroying the other's in-progress work. Currently, `rtl_enforce` resets `ROOT HEAD` if it detects changes, which orphans any peer's commits if multiple sessions run on the same clone.
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md-23-
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md-24-## Bet / Blast Radius / Reversibility
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md:25:**Bet:** A simple `mkdir`-based directory lock in the two driver entrypoints (`marathon-drive.sh` and `relay-drive.sh`) is sufficient to prevent concurrent execution on the same clone without changing the underlying `rtl_enforce` behavior.
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md:26:**Tradeoff:** We block valid concurrent non-mutating reads if they use these entrypoints, but safety is paramount.
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md-27-**Failure mode:** If a process crashes without triggering `trap EXIT`, the `.git/relay-driver.lock` might be left behind, requiring manual removal.
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md-28-**Reversibility:** Easy. Can be reverted without touching coordination logs.
--
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md-36-
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md-37-## Fix
PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-42-CONCURRENT-RELAY-ROOT-HEAD.md:38:Implement a single-writer guard using a repo-level lock (`.git/relay-driver.lock`) inside the drivers (`marathon-drive.sh` and `relay-drive.sh`). If the lock is held, the driver will immediately exit with a clear error, preventing concurrent runs on the same clone.

utils/swarm-preflight.sh-23-# utils/swarm-preflight.sh — one durable intake planner for marathon runs (GH-25).
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-24-#
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-25-# Turns EITHER a single project doc OR an explicit bundle of GitHub issues into a
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:26:# marathon-ready run packet: it normalizes both inputs into one shape, checks branch
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-27-# freshness, proves the fix is still required, gates remediation readiness, assigns
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:28:# Codex/agy lanes, and emits a self-contained packet the orchestrator hands to
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:29:# relay-automation/marathon-drive.sh. It is the PRODUCER of the packet, never the
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-30-# executor of the marathon (GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md §8 — the operator decides).
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-31-#
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-32-# The planner reads the EXECUTION SURFACE OF RECORD, never a raw issue thread
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-33-# (GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md §11): every --gh-issue must already have an in-repo GH-* capture
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-34-# doc, and that doc must carry a machine-readable preflight contract. The contract is a
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-35-# single fenced ```json block under a heading matching /preflight contract/i, e.g.:
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-36-#
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:37:#     ## Swarm Preflight Contract
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-38-#     ```json
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-39-#     {
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-40-#       "target":      { "repo": ".", "ref": "main" },
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-41-#       "gate":        "bash validate.sh",
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-42-#       "fix_probes":  [ { "type": "path_absent", "path": "utils/swarm-preflight.sh" } ],
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:43:#       "artifacts":   [ "utils/swarm-preflight.sh", "test/swarm-preflight.sh" ],
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-44-#       "remediation": { "source": "self#phases", "criteria": "Phases 1-7 of GH-25" },
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-45-#       "lanes":       { "agy_safe": [], "orchestrator_only": [ "bin/", ".tick/" ] }
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-46-#     }
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-47-#     ```
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-48-#
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-49-# Usage:
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-50-#   utils/swarm-preflight.sh --project-doc PROJECT/2-WORKING/GH-25-*.md
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-51-#   utils/swarm-preflight.sh --gh-issue 25 --gh-issue 26 [--target-root REPO]
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:52:#   utils/swarm-preflight.sh --project-doc DOC --dry-run        # checks only, no packet written
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-53-#
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:54:# Exit: 0 ready (packet emitted) · 2 usage · 3 contract missing/invalid ·
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-55-#       4 stale/already-landed (fix not required) · 5 not marathon-ready ·
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-56-#       6 blocked/missing-target · 7 ambiguous.
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-57-#
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:58:# Branch prompt (GH-69) — orchestrating-agent contract: a ready packet's provenance carries
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-59-# `suggested_branch` (deterministic: marathon/<slug>-<run-date>) and `branch_ready` (does it already
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-60-# exist?). If `branch_ready: false` and `skip_branch_prompt: false`, ASK THE OPERATOR before invoking
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-61-# marathon-drive.sh — "This lane will commit to <branch>. Suggested branch: <suggested_branch>. Cut it
utils/swarm-preflight.sh-62-# now? [yes / no / custom name]" (never auto-cut — GUIDING-PRINCIPLES.md §8). `skip_branch_prompt: true`
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:63:# (risk==1 in the doc frontmatter AND an independent-zone artifact set — no kernel/shim path) means
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:64:# proceed on the current branch without asking. packet.md/packet.json both carry these fields inline,
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:65:# and the packet.md "Suggested branch" line already states which of the two applies — a driving agent
utils/swarm-preflight.sh:66:# reading the packet doesn't need to recompute it.

     1	# MARATHON.yaml — 2026-08-10: release 0.3.0 Nightwatch, wave 1.
     2	#
     3	# ONE phase. That is not a shortage of candidates — it is the honest output of the write-set
     4	# analysis below, and the number is the finding.
     5	#
     6	# This run doubles as the first dogfood of the GH-484 revised marathon system: phase output lands in
     7	# `marathon-system/` (the new default) rather than `phases/`, exercised via the DEFAULT rather than
     8	# an explicit `--phases-dir`, because a default nobody exercises is not a default.
     9	#
    10	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    11	# WHY ONLY ONE LANE — the self-modification constraint, applied to the Nightwatch manifest
    12	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    13	# Nightwatch's theme is the harness's own run lifecycle, so nearly every manifest member is a change
    14	# TO THE MACHINERY THE MARATHON RUNS ON. Litmus wave 2 wrote this constraint down; Nightwatch is
    15	# where it bites hardest. Write-sets below are taken from each capture doc's
    16	# `## Swarm Preflight Contract` artifacts list, read on 2026-08-10 — not from memory.
    17	#
    18	#   #388  run-log durability
    19	#         artifacts: relay-automation/marathon.sh, utils/py/marathon_drive.py, utils/py/rtl.py, …
    20	#         EXCLUDED. `marathon.sh` is the outer driver EXECUTING the chain, and bash reads a script by
    21	#         byte offset as it goes — committing a rewrite mid-run can corrupt the remainder in a way
    22	#         that presents as anything but its cause. `rtl.py` is the turn kernel on top of that.
    23	#
    24	#   #426  worktree isolation leak
    25	#         artifacts: relay-automation/relay-turn-lib.sh, utils/py/rtl.py, …
    26	#         EXCLUDED. The turn kernel, sourced fresh by EVERY turn.
    27	#         Worth stating because it is the tempting one: #426 is a true Nightwatch blocker per #431,
    28	#         and the obvious workaround — "run it as a single phase, so a wedge costs nothing
    29	#         downstream" — DOES NOT WORK. A phase is not one turn. The builder turn commits, then the
    30	#         REVIEWER turn re-sources the kernel from the working tree, plus up to
    31	#         `max_review_rounds` more. A broken kernel wedges the reviewer inside its own phase.
    32	#         Single-phase isolation contains a DRIVER change; it does not contain a KERNEL change.
    33	#
    34	#   #409 + #408  leaked tick claim / discarded stderr
    35	#         EXCLUDED, and not preflightable regardless: `GH-409-408-TOKEN-FAILURE-VISIBILITY.md` still
    36	#         carries no `## Swarm Preflight Contract`, so per GUIDING-PRINCIPLES §11 it cannot be
    37	#         verdicted. Its deliverables are `rtl.py`, the five turn shims, and `tick claim`'s exit
    38	#         semantics — the claim/handoff primitive the driver uses between phases.
    39	#
    40	#   #354  concurrent swarms (Phase 1 containment)
    41	#         EXCLUDED. `GH-354-CONCURRENT-SWARMS.md` has no preflight contract either. Not verdictable.
    42	#
    43	#   #358  lock-flake instrumentation                                   → THE LANE BELOW
    44	#
    45	# So of the six named manifest members, two cannot be preflighted at all, three are excluded on the
    46	# self-modification constraint, and one is buildable. A marathon cannot close the Nightwatch
    47	# milestone — same conclusion Litmus reached, for the same structural reason, and it should be
    48	# recorded now rather than rediscovered at freeze time.
    49	#
    50	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    51	# WHY #358 IS IN, WHEN LITMUS WAVE 2 EXCLUDED IT
    52	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    53	# Litmus wave 2 excluded #358 with: "Edits `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; changing CI from inside an
    54	# unattended marathon is a risk this release does not need to take."
    55	#
    56	# That reason is correct and it applies to **Phase 2, not Phase 1**. The capture doc's own phase
    57	# table puts `.github/workflows/ci.yml` in Phase 2 (disposition) and Phase 1's artifacts are
    58	# `test/xyz-completion.sh`, `utils/telemetry/append-xyz-completion.sh`,
    59	# `test/gh358-lock-instrumentation.sh`. Phase 1 is CI-free.
    60	#
    61	# Firing Phase 1 alone is additionally what the doc DEMANDS, not merely what it permits:
    62	#   "Phase 2 must not be pre-committed in the packet. A builder told which disposition to apply will
    63	#    produce instrumentation that agrees with the instruction."
    64	# A two-phase run of this lane would be an acceptance violation, not an efficiency.
    65	#
    66	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    67	# THE ONE LIVE-PATH EXPOSURE, AND ITS CONTAINMENT
    68	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    69	# `utils/telemetry/append-xyz-completion.sh` is in Phase 1's write-set AND is invoked by the driver
    70	# running this phase — `relay-automation/marathon.sh:69` and `utils/py/marathon_drive.py:656` both
    71	# resolve it as the GH-75 end-of-run completion writer. A grep of the brief's artifact list against
    72	# "driver code" would not surface this: the file is telemetry, not driver, and the coupling is an
    73	# env-var default, not a call site in the driver's own text.
    74	#
    75	# Contained by pinning `XYZ_APPEND_BIN` to a PRE-RUN SNAPSHOT of the script, so the running marathon
    76	# executes the frozen copy no matter what the builder does to the tree. Both the bash and Python
    77	# drivers already honour `XYZ_APPEND_BIN` as an override, so this needs no code change.
    78	#
    79	# The exposure was mild even uncontained — one call, at completion, after all work is committed and
    80	# gated — but "mild" is a judgement and a snapshot is a fact.
    81	#
    82	# OPERATOR GO GIVEN 2026-08-10, after being shown the one-lane finding above and the reason #426
    83	# cannot be rescued by single-phase isolation. Closeout: `--closeout-pr` (open, never merge).
    84	#
    85	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    86	# PREFLIGHT — re-run 2026-08-10 against development @ e25c064ef
    87	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    88	#   lane   verdict           acceptance fidelity           issue-state   source-url
    89	#   gh358  ready (exit 0)    match 7/7 verbatim            OPEN          ok → issue #358
    90	#
    91	#   freshness: fetch_ok=1 upstream=origin/development ahead=0 behind=0
    92	#   `dirty=1` is reported and is accounted for: the working tree carries 8 untracked paths, all
    93	#   under PROJECT/1-INBOX/, phases/ (stale pre-GH-484 run output) and relay-system/. None is in the
    94	#   lane's write-set and none is harness source.
    95	#
    96	# Builder is codex (GH-212, subscription-billed). Reviewer is agy, so the reviewer is never the model
    97	# that wrote the change.
    98	#
    99	# Parent capture doc:

   111	    turn_timeout_s: 900
   112	    max_review_rounds: 3
    90	- **Do not** raise a bound, add a retry, or otherwise *dispose* of the flake.
    91	
    92	Ship the instrumentation and the controls. The disposition is chosen later, from the evidence your
    93	change produces.
    94	
    95	## Hard non-goals (from the capture doc)
    96	
    97	- **`M` stays 16.** Lowering it makes the symptom vanish and leaves the safety property untested.
    98	- **The distinctness check stays**, for the same reason.
    99	- **Do not treat this as an ordinary flake.** A flaky *lock* test is the one kind that cannot be
   100	  waved off.
   101	
   102	## Write-set
   103	
   104	| File | Note |
   105	|---|---|
   106	| `test/xyz-completion.sh` | the failing test — both `wait` loops |
   107	| `utils/telemetry/append-xyz-completion.sh` | the writer; retain/propagate exit status |
   108	| `test/gh358-lock-instrumentation.sh` | **new** — the two negative controls |
   109	| `validate.sh` | register the new test in `TESTS=()`; it does **not** glob `test/` |
   110	
   111	Nothing else. In particular `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is **out of scope for this phase**.
   112	
   113	## One containment note you should know about
   114	
   115	`utils/telemetry/append-xyz-completion.sh` is in your write-set **and** is invoked by the marathon
   116	driver running this very phase (`relay-automation/marathon.sh:69`, `utils/py/marathon_drive.py:656`)
   117	to write its end-of-run completion record. The run pins `XYZ_APPEND_BIN` to a **pre-run snapshot** of
   118	that script, so your edits cannot affect the run that is building them.
   119	
   120	That containment protects the run, not you: it does not license a change that breaks the appender's
   121	normal contract. Keep the CLI signature and exit semantics compatible.

README.md-143-
README.md-144-- **Runtime — Python by default.** The harness entry points run their **Python** implementation by
README.md-145-  default. Every shim keeps its original Bash body inline as the escape hatch, so you can force the
README.md:146:  legacy Bash path at any granularity: one command with `XYZ_PYTHON=0 <command>`, a whole session or
README.md-147-  CI job with `export XYZ_PYTHON=0`, or permanently with `git revert <flip-sha>` (the flip is one
README.md-148-  isolated commit). Python 3.8+ is required; if `python3` is missing or too old a shim prints a warning
README.md-149-  and falls back to Bash on its own.

README.md-273-- `relay-system/` — relay transcripts, reviews, and dogfood runs.
README.md-274-- `PROJECT/2-WORKING/` — active project docs and working plans.
README.md:275:- `bin/tick`, `src/`, `test/` — the `tick` coordination kernel and its test suite.
README.md-276-- `utils/swarm-preflight.sh` — marathon intake planner: turns a project doc or a GH-issue bundle into a marathon-ready run packet (freshness + fix-still-required checks, readiness gate, Codex/agy lane plan). Run `utils/swarm-preflight.sh --help`; see [GH-25-SWARM-PREFLIGHT-PLANNER.md](PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-25-SWARM-PREFLIGHT-PLANNER.md).
README.md-277-- `utils/marathon-plan.sh` — the marathon planner/ranker: scores the whole ROADMAP ledger into waves of disjoint, collision-safe write-sets, and with `--deep` delegates to `swarm-preflight.sh --dry-run` per item for an authoritative freshness verdict. Writes `PROJECT/2-WORKING/MARATHON-PLAN-<date>.md` — the "marathon file" the operator skills act on.
README.md:278:- `utils/swe-diagram/` — dependency-free architecture/Git-history diagram generator; `layout: "git-lanes"` renders stacked branch lanes with commits left-to-right, driven by a local ref-reading generator that emits an auditable JSON spec plus self-contained HTML. See [GH-201](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/201).
README.md-279-- `utils/git-bundle-snapshot.sh` + `relay-automation/hooks/gh177-sandbox-test-guard.sh` — the wipe-prevention layer: rotated `git bundle --all` backups on a daily cron, plus a PreToolUse hook that blocks running the test suite under a *sandboxed* Claude Code Bash call (the ignition for the GH-177 repo wipes). See [GH-233](https://github.com/Claude-AI-Tools-Ventura-County/xyz-3-agents-swarm/issues/233).
README.md-280-- `install.sh` — materializes the `tick` runtime (`bin/tick` + `src/*.js`) into an external repo and records the install in a per-user, machine-local registry (`~/.config/xyz/registry.tsv`). See "Install into another repo" below.
README.md-281-- `utils/hq/` — **HQ**, the multi-repo command center (`hq.sh` + `hq-lib.sh`); driven by the user-level `/hq` skill in `skills/hq/`. See [HQ — multi-repo command center](#hq--multi-repo-command-center) below.

relay-automation/agy-turn.sh-66-#   RELAY_TURN_TIMEOUT_S — per-turn wall-clock ceiling in seconds (default: 900). A hung or

relay-automation/agy-turn.sh-70-#   (a) SILENT FAILURE UNDER A SANDBOX — when agy's backend network is blocked (e.g. Claude Code's
relay-automation/agy-turn.sh-71-#       Bash sandbox) `agy -p` exits 0 with EMPTY output. An empty "successful" turn is a FALSE
relay-automation/agy-turn.sh-72-#       success for an automated relay, so we treat empty-output-on-exit-0 as a hard failure (exit 5).
relay-automation/agy-turn.sh:73:#       Run this shim with the sandbox OFF (like codex; memory: codex-cli-needs-sandbox-disabled).
relay-automation/agy-turn.sh-74-#   (b) NO JSON / TOKEN OUTPUT — agy print mode has no `-o json` and no usage block, so there is NO
relay-automation/agy-turn.sh-75-#       cost.tokens capture here (an agy lane is cost-blind — a floor, same Phase-1 partial as Codex).
relay-automation/agy-turn.sh-76-#

Also fixed two `[Should]` findings both models converged on: `MARATHON_TMP` cleanup now uses an EXIT trap instead of one `rm -f` at the end (survives an unexpected early abort); added a `MARATHON_SCAN_BIN` test seam + a real failure-path test. `test/hq-rollup.sh` extended to 21/21 (4 cases: populated ROADMAP, empty ROADMAP, marathon-scan.sh failing, agy entirely absent). Full `bash validate.sh` re-run: still only the 2 pre-existing unrelated reds. Re-dogfooded live against the operator's real vault once more. `pdda.sh run` clean. | All 4 phases complete. Merge PR #196 to `main`, then close #192. |

PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md-14-Where they fundamentally diverge
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md-15-The two "multi-agent" stories are not the same thing:
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md-16-
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md:17:Eve = a framework/SDK to build one durable agent product, where a root agent delegates to its own subagents and talks to Slack/Discord/HTTP channels. The agents are cooperative and framework-coordinated. Hosted, vendor stack.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md-18-This repo = a coordination spike to make separately-owned, heterogeneous vendor CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini) work concurrently on one shared git repo without colliding. Local-transport only, no accounts, no remote dependency.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md-19-The load-bearing piece of this project — tick claim with O_EXCL locks, drift detection, file-collision analysis, the honest-concurrency metric — has no analog in Eve, because Eve never has two independently-owned agents racing for the same file. Its subagents are conducted; yours are negotiated.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md-20-
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md-21-Bottom line
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md:22:They share a design philosophy (filesystem-first, durable, hook/skill/schedule primitives) but live at different layers: Eve is "how to build a durable agent"; this repo is "how to keep N agents you didn't build from stepping on each other." Eve is the closest mainstream framework to your aesthetic — but it assumes away the exact problem (tick's collision-free claims across heterogeneous agents) that this spike exists to solve.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md-23-
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/INITIAL-COMPARISON.md:24:Want me to pull the actual Eve subagent/sandbox API pages and do a deeper primitive-by-primitive map (e.g. could tick sit under an Eve-style framework, or is it a competitor)?
--

PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-13-## 0. One-paragraph charter
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-14-
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-15-Eve (Apache-2.0, local clone at `$EVE_REPO`, indexed by Ask Self code RAG) is the
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md:16:closest mainstream framework to this repo's *aesthetic*: filesystem-first, durable,
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-17-hook/skill/schedule-shaped agent substrate. This study mines Eve for **durable, high-level
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-18-patterns** — ideas and designs, not code — and lands them as reusable learning artifacts we
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-19-can apply to `tick` and `relay-automation`. **We copy zero code.** Ideas and architecture
--
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-101-  1. RAG-survey: directory layout, the primitive set (instructions / agent.ts / tools / skills / channels /
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-102-     connections / subagents / sandbox / hooks / schedules), and how they're discovered/wired.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-103-  2. Identify the *seams*: where durability, delegation, isolation, and filesystem-convention each live.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md:104:  3. Write `10-ARCHITECTURE-MAP.md` as prose + our own diagrams. Pointers to Eve files allowed; content not.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-105-- **Output:** `10-ARCHITECTURE-MAP.md`.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-106-- **Exit gate / QA:**
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-107-  - [ ] Every Eve primitive named and explained in one paragraph each, in our words.
--
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-148-- **Objective:** convert patterns into decisions about *our* codebase.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-149-- **Inputs:** the four deep-dive files.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-150-- **Steps:**
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md:151:  1. For each durable pattern, map to concrete surfaces: `tick` kernel, `relay-automation` loop, `marathon`,
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-152-     skills, decision-record flow.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-153-  2. Classify each: **Adopt** (clear win, low risk) / **Adapt** (good idea, needs reshaping for us) /
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-154-     **Reject** (doesn't fit — record *why*, so we don't relitigate).
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-155-  3. For Adopt/Adapt, sketch the *independent* re-derivation at a high level (no Eve code referenced in the sketch).
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md:156:  4. Flag blast-radius for anything touching the `tick` kernel or the event-log format (those are load-bearing).
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-157-- **Output:** `30-APPLICABILITY.md` — a ranked table: pattern · surface · adopt/adapt/reject · rationale · blast radius.

PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-159-  - [ ] Every Phase-2 pattern classified with a one-line rationale.

PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-164-### Phase 4 — Housing the artifacts (catalog + decision records)
--
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-168-  1. Distill `LESSONS.md` — the living catalog: every durable pattern, in our words, with its
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-169-     applicability verdict and a one-line "so what for us." This is the canonical takeaway doc.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-170-  2. Write a decision record in `decisions/` **only for high-impact adoptions** — anything that touches the
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md:171:     `tick` kernel, the event-log format, or the `relay-automation` contract. Lower-impact Adopt/Adapt items
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-172-     live in `LESSONS.md` only (no ADR overhead). Use this repo's record format (status / date / reversibility /
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-173-     revisit / the bet / rejected / expected signal). One file per high-impact pattern.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-174-  3. Cross-link: `LESSONS.md` → decision records; decision records → `20-patterns/*` provenance.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-175-  4. Convert any "later" items into `BACKLOG.md` entries so nothing dangles.
PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md:176:  5. Update repo memory (a `project` memory: "Eve study lives in PROJECT/2-WORKING/EVE-STUDY; lessons in LESSONS.md").

PROJECT/1-INBOX/EVE-STUDY/EVE-REVIEW.md-179-  - [ ] `LESSONS.md` is self-contained — a reader who never saw Eve understands each pattern and why it matters to us.

PROJECT/3-COMPLETED/GH-209-MARATHON-ROOT-LEAK-AUDIT.md:40:| Capture written; scope explicitly narrowed after finding the full architectural fix is not safely automatable (see Decision). Confirmed with operator via the marathon-scope selection. **New live evidence for the Problem, found running today's own marathon (2026-07-16):** phase `gh213`'s pre-advance gate command (`bash test/find-harness.sh && bash test/marathon.sh && ...`) ran nested INSIDE the still-live outer `marathon-drive.sh` process, and `test/marathon.sh`'s GH-205 resume sub-case failed there (`grep: .../phases/gh205/RELAY.md: No such file or directory`) despite passing 33/33 standalone immediately before and after. Confirmed by reproduction attempts with matching env vars (`TICK_REPO_ROOT`, `MARATHON_ROOT`, `MARATHON_BUILDER`/`REVIEWER`, `CODEX_AGENT`/`AGY_AGENT`, `RELAY_DRIVER_LOCKED=1`) that this specific set does NOT reproduce it standalone — the exact leak vector is still unidentified, but the phenomenon (nesting `test/marathon.sh`/`test/marathon-drive.sh` inside a live `marathon-drive.sh` process is unreliable) is now directly demonstrated, not just inferred from the original incident. Worked around today by not nesting those two test files in the marathon's own `--pre-advance-cmd` (verified standalone by the orchestrator instead). **The exact leak vector was found and fixed by this very phase's builder turn**: `MARATHON_LANE_NS` (set by the outer `marathon.sh`/`marathon-drive.sh` for the live phase) was leaking into `test/marathon.sh`/`test/marathon-drive.sh`'s own nested invocations of the real scripts, redirecting rendered relay paths under the outer phase's namespaced directory and breaking pre-existing path assertions — fixed with `unset MARATHON_LANE_NS` at the top of both test files (GH-207's own explicit namespaced test cases still set it per-invocation and remain covered). New `test/marathon-root-audit.sh` (13/13, registered in `validate.sh`) statically audits that every real-script invocation in the test suite is `MARATHON_ROOT`-scoped or fixture-local, going forward. Reviewed and Approved by agy (tick token confirmed `status: done`), but agy-turn.sh's isolation-breach detector then failed the TURN on a known false positive (GH-183, already tracked, unfixed) — the relay file's Approved content was committed by hand after independently re-verifying `test/marathon-root-audit.sh` (13/13), `test/marathon.sh` (33/33), `test/marathon-drive.sh` (85/85), and full `validate.sh` (green except the pre-existing #208). | Done. Continuing to `gh203`. |

PROJECT/1-INBOX/AIDER-STRUCTURE-RESEARCH.md-119-Aider's troubleshooting page emphasizes that above ~25k tokens of context, most models "start to become distracted and become less likely to conform to their system prompt". Local model servers (LM Studio, Ollama) often default to very small context windows that silently truncate Aider's prompts. [aider](https://aider.chat/docs/troubleshooting/edit-errors.html)
PROJECT/1-INBOX/AIDER-STRUCTURE-RESEARCH.md-120-
PROJECT/1-INBOX/AIDER-STRUCTURE-RESEARCH.md:121:In LM Studio, explicitly set the context length in the model load settings (e.g., 32768 or 65536 depending on your RAM). Then match it in `.aider.model.metadata.json` and `.aider.conf.yml` as shown above. Mismatches between the server's context window and what Aider thinks it has will cause silent truncation.

277:# GH-457: the gate's caps come from a TIER, because one wall cap cannot serve both jobs.
278-#
279-# The single 900s cap stopped meaning anything. Measured on one host inside 24 hours, same suite:
280-#
281-#     2026-08-07              ~704-806s
282-#     2026-08-08 evening       878.8s wall / 532.5s CPU   (loaded, 60% CPU)
283:#     2026-08-08 marathon r3    957s                      (in-marathon, real gate invocation)
284-#     shipped caps              900s wall / 600s CPU
285-#
286-# The suite did not grow ~250s in a day; that drift is machine contention. So a 900s cap was
287-# measuring how busy the laptop was, which is not a property of the change under test — and a fully
288:# GREEN validate.sh returned `gate-killed` (108) at the default, a resource kill dressed as a
289-# verdict, which is exactly #407's failure mode. Both Litmus wave-2 runs had to pass a run-time
290-# override to avoid it, and a guard that always needs an override is a speed bump that only fires
291-# when someone forgets.

   118	## `marathon.sh` roots
   119	
   120	`marathon.sh` resolves two different roots on purpose:
   121	
   122	- `MARATHON_HOME`: the harness install that owns `bin/tick`, `bin/marathon-yaml`, and telemetry helpers. Default: the script's own parent dir (`relay-automation/..`).
   123	- `MARATHON_ROOT`: the target repo that owns the plan's `brief:` files, `marathon-system/`, `.tick/`, and commit target. Default: `git -C "$PWD" rev-parse --show-toplevel`; outside a git repo it falls back to `MARATHON_HOME`.
   124	
   125	That split preserves dev-checkout behavior (`MARATHON_HOME == MARATHON_ROOT`) and makes vendored installs work with no bin overrides:
   126	
   127	```bash
   128	cd /path/to/target-repo
   129	./.xyz/relay-automation/marathon.sh --plan marathon-plans/my-wave/MARATHON.yaml
   130	```
   131	
   132	Override them independently only when you genuinely need a non-default harness or repo root. The lower-level binary overrides (`TICK_BIN`, `MARATHON_YAML_BIN`, `XYZ_APPEND_BIN`) still win if set.
   133	
   134	## `marathon-plan.sh` zone config
   135	
   136	`utils/marathon-plan.sh` can now load a repo-specific zone model instead of hardcoding xyz's own
   137	`kernel` / `shim` filenames:
   138	
   139	- Resolution order: `--zones-config <file>` → `QUEUE_PLAN_ZONES_FILE` → `QUEUE_PLAN_ROOT/.marathon-plan-zones.json` → built-in `utils/marathon-plan-zones.default.json`.
   140	- Explicit files fail loud on read/JSON/schema errors; only an absent root-local file falls through.

## ANSWER

Do not publish either draft unchanged. #391 has two material false premises (`bin/marathon-yaml`’s required fields; `depends_on` preserving parallelism). #392 leaves “Path A” undefined and cannot make its 7-lane conclusion defensible from the stated measurements.

## FINDINGS

### #392

1. [Should] “Requirement” needs a defined workload and a stated recommended minimum. Otherwise a builder can add “Recommended: 16 GB” and pass without saying which mode, agents, or host reserve that recommendation covers. The current Prerequisites section indeed has no hardware number. [README.md](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/README.md:129)

2. [Blocker] `Path A` is undefined in this context. It does not appear in the README’s execution-mode vocabulary, so “16 GB … Path A only” is neither reviewable nor safely implementable. Define each path by exact command/mode and concurrency.

3. [Blocker] The 2.2 GB / 1.5–2 GB claims have no source or measurement method in the repository, and the arithmetic cannot size a wave when “whatever the target repo’s suite needs” is unbounded. Require: host/spec, builder/reviewer mix, observed peak versus steady RSS, measured command, available-memory reserve, and an explicit formula/caveat.

4. [Should] Attribution plus date is not enough to make a result re-measurable; it can be satisfied by an opaque sentence. Require a committed/raw measurement artifact or reproducible command and harness revision. “Unattributed number cannot be re-measured” is also too absolute.

5. [Should] The outcome is right—`kernel.maxPerWave: 1` is not a RAM limit—but “write-conflict rule” is imprecise. The implementation has both exact write-set collision detection and an independent zone cap; kernel lanes are capped even without an exact path collision. Say “coordination/containment zone cap, not a memory cap.” [marathon-plan-zones.default.json](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/marathon-plan-zones.default.json:4) [\_marathon_plan.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/_marathon_plan.py:1013)

6. [Should] Narrow “no clamp.” The harness has an RSS guard that kills an over-budget *gate*; it does not probe host RAM or calculate/refuse a lane width. The present wording can falsely imply no memory protection exists. [marathon_drive.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/marathon_drive.py:1362)

7. [Blocker] “A 16 GB host can determine whether a 7-lane parallel wave is supported” is satisfiable by simply declaring it unsupported, and is not derivable from the stated figures because suite memory and baseline reserve are unspecified. Define “supported,” wave composition, and the conservative calculation.

Missing scope lock: require a docs-only diff/allowlist (README plus any explicitly named measurement evidence) so a builder cannot add a probe “to support” the prose.

### #391

1. [Blocker] The input model is unspecified. `marathon-plan` generates a scheduling overlay from ROADMAP; preflight generates one packet directory per doc/bundle. Neither creates the required plan-lane ↔ packet mapping. A cheap fake can emit a one-phase YAML from any packet. Require exact matching identity (issue/slug), expected phase count, rejection of missing/extra/duplicate packets, and output location. [marathon_plan.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/marathon_plan.py:126) [swarm_preflight.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/swarm_preflight.py:1461)

2. [Should] Keeping `bin/marathon-yaml` unchanged is coherent, but it is not the complete runtime oracle: it does not require a `brief` or `artifact`. Retain this criterion, then add `marathon.sh --dry-run` as the second, unchanged-runtime acceptance gate. [marathon-yaml](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/bin/marathon-yaml:92) [marathon.sh](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/relay-automation/marathon.sh:193)

3. [Blocker] False premise: the validator requires only `id` and `reviewer`; `brief` and `artifact` are optional to it. It also derives order from authored `depends_on`, not from a “lane ranking.” Rewrite this as an emitter contract, not a validator fact. [marathon-yaml](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/bin/marathon-yaml:92)

4. [Should] Explicit `--reviewer` is good, but require the emitted value to be the supplied value and validator-acceptable. “The issue identifies [it] as not derivable” is not verifiable from the artifact and should be removed.

5. [Blocker] False premise: `MARATHON.yaml` is strictly serial. Omitting `depends_on` does not permit parallelism; adding it everywhere cannot “remove all parallelism.” The criterion should instead require emitted dependencies to preserve the declared causal/order relation, with scalar-only dependency limits handled explicitly. [MARATHON.example.yaml](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml:7)

6. [Should] Missing-packet rejection is necessary but incomplete: reject malformed, stale, duplicate, wrong-lane, and packet/plan artifact mismatches too. Note that a later missing brief can be discovered only after earlier phases have run, because `marathon.sh` checks each brief inside its phase loop. [marathon.sh](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/relay-automation/marathon.sh:186)

7. [Pass] Fine.

8. [Should] This contradicts “emitter only” unless scope is renamed “emitter plus generated firing guidance.” Requiring merely that `marathon.sh` is named is weak; require the generated document to print the exact multi-phase command and its required inputs. Today it only directs operators to `swarm-preflight → marathon-drive`. [\_marathon_plan.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/_marathon_plan.py:1317)

A further #391 omission: “brief from packet path” conflicts with the project convention that a real plan and phase briefs live under `PROJECT/2-WORKING/<capture>/`; default preflight packets live under a transcript/preflight directory. Require a generated/copyable stable brief under the plan directory, or explicitly change that convention. [MARATHON.example.yaml](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml:22) [swarm_preflight.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/swarm_preflight.py:1445)

## Extra answers

- #391 validator freeze: coherent. Do not change `bin/marathon-yaml`; add the unchanged validator plus `marathon.sh --dry-run` as independent checks.
- Home: use a separate Python emitter, not `marathon-plan --emit-yaml`. The planner is a ROADMAP scheduling overlay; the emitter consumes packet material and produces an executable manifest, a distinct boundary.

## ANSWER

Do not publish either draft unchanged. #391 has two material false premises (`bin/marathon-yaml`’s required fields; `depends_on` preserving parallelism). #392 leaves “Path A” undefined and cannot make its 7-lane conclusion defensible from the stated measurements.

## FINDINGS

### #392

1. [Should] “Requirement” needs a defined workload and a stated recommended minimum. Otherwise a builder can add “Recommended: 16 GB” and pass without saying which mode, agents, or host reserve that recommendation covers. The current Prerequisites section indeed has no hardware number. [README.md](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/README.md:129)

2. [Blocker] `Path A` is undefined in this context. It does not appear in the README’s execution-mode vocabulary, so “16 GB … Path A only” is neither reviewable nor safely implementable. Define each path by exact command/mode and concurrency.

3. [Blocker] The 2.2 GB / 1.5–2 GB claims have no source or measurement method in the repository, and the arithmetic cannot size a wave when “whatever the target repo’s suite needs” is unbounded. Require: host/spec, builder/reviewer mix, observed peak versus steady RSS, measured command, available-memory reserve, and an explicit formula/caveat.

4. [Should] Attribution plus date is not enough to make a result re-measurable; it can be satisfied by an opaque sentence. Require a committed/raw measurement artifact or reproducible command and harness revision. “Unattributed number cannot be re-measured” is also too absolute.

5. [Should] The outcome is right—`kernel.maxPerWave: 1` is not a RAM limit—but “write-conflict rule” is imprecise. The implementation has both exact write-set collision detection and an independent zone cap; kernel lanes are capped even without an exact path collision. Say “coordination/containment zone cap, not a memory cap.” [marathon-plan-zones.default.json](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/marathon-plan-zones.default.json:4) [\_marathon_plan.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/_marathon_plan.py:1013)

6. [Should] Narrow “no clamp.” The harness has an RSS guard that kills an over-budget *gate*; it does not probe host RAM or calculate/refuse a lane width. The present wording can falsely imply no memory protection exists. [marathon_drive.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/marathon_drive.py:1362)

7. [Blocker] “A 16 GB host can determine whether a 7-lane parallel wave is supported” is satisfiable by simply declaring it unsupported, and is not derivable from the stated figures because suite memory and baseline reserve are unspecified. Define “supported,” wave composition, and the conservative calculation.

Missing scope lock: require a docs-only diff/allowlist (README plus any explicitly named measurement evidence) so a builder cannot add a probe “to support” the prose.

### #391

1. [Blocker] The input model is unspecified. `marathon-plan` generates a scheduling overlay from ROADMAP; preflight generates one packet directory per doc/bundle. Neither creates the required plan-lane ↔ packet mapping. A cheap fake can emit a one-phase YAML from any packet. Require exact matching identity (issue/slug), expected phase count, rejection of missing/extra/duplicate packets, and output location. [marathon_plan.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/marathon_plan.py:126) [swarm_preflight.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/swarm_preflight.py:1461)

2. [Should] Keeping `bin/marathon-yaml` unchanged is coherent, but it is not the complete runtime oracle: it does not require a `brief` or `artifact`. Retain this criterion, then add `marathon.sh --dry-run` as the second, unchanged-runtime acceptance gate. [marathon-yaml](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/bin/marathon-yaml:92) [marathon.sh](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/relay-automation/marathon.sh:193)

3. [Blocker] False premise: the validator requires only `id` and `reviewer`; `brief` and `artifact` are optional to it. It also derives order from authored `depends_on`, not from a “lane ranking.” Rewrite this as an emitter contract, not a validator fact. [marathon-yaml](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/bin/marathon-yaml:92)

4. [Should] Explicit `--reviewer` is good, but require the emitted value to be the supplied value and validator-acceptable. “The issue identifies [it] as not derivable” is not verifiable from the artifact and should be removed.

5. [Blocker] False premise: `MARATHON.yaml` is strictly serial. Omitting `depends_on` does not permit parallelism; adding it everywhere cannot “remove all parallelism.” The criterion should instead require emitted dependencies to preserve the declared causal/order relation, with scalar-only dependency limits handled explicitly. [MARATHON.example.yaml](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/relay-automation/MARATHON.example.yaml:7)

6. [Should] Missing-packet rejection is necessary but incomplete: reject malformed, stale, duplicate, wrong-lane, and packet/plan artifact mismatches too. Note that a later missing brief can be discovered only after earlier phases have run, because `marathon.sh` checks each brief inside its phase loop. [marathon.sh](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/relay-automation/marathon.sh:186)

7. [Pass] Fine.

8. [Should] This contradicts “emitter only” unless scope is renamed “emitter plus generated firing guidance.” Requiring merely that `marathon.sh` is named is weak; require the generated document to print the exact multi-phase command and its required inputs. Today it only directs operators to `swarm-preflight → marathon-drive`. [\_marathon_plan.py](/private/var/folders/69/3l_82qtj7fzglnt_jjg07jh40000gn/T/consult-wt-94630-bvhtc39m/utils/py/_marathon_plan.py:1317)

A further #391 omission: “brief from packet path” conflicts with the project convention that a real plan and phase briefs live under `PROJECT/2-WORKING/<capture>/`; default preflight packets live under a transcript/preflight directory. Require a generated/copyable stable brief under the plan directory, or explicitly change that convention.
